title: Mutable segment snapshot assertion fails after crash recovery: ctid_set.len() != expected_ctids
body:
Running `pdb.verify_index` on a healthy-looking index shortly after fault recovery (container kill/restart of the postgres pod), with no concurrent writers, intermittently fails:

```
ERROR:  assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 20
 right: 2
(SQLState XX000)
```

Backtrace (from log_error_verbosity=VERBOSE):

```
SegmentMetaEntry::mutable_snapshot          pg_search/src/postgres/storage/block.rs:520
  (assert_eq!(ctid_set.len(), expected_ctids as usize))
index_memory_segment                        pg_search/src/index/directory/mvcc.rs:719
MVCCDirectory::file_entry                   pg_search/src/index/directory/mvcc.rs:221
MVCCDirectory::get_file_handle -> open_read
SegmentReader::fast_fields_readers          (tantivy)
```

Observations:

- Replaying the first `max_doc + num_deleted_docs` entries of the mutable segment yields 20 live ctids; the header's `max_doc - num_deleted_docs` expects 2.
- The error repeats for a while, then clears on its own: a later `pdb.verify_index` on the same index passes with no intervening writes.
- The workload is stopped when the check runs, so this is not the concurrent-writer race in #5913.
- The failing frame is a general read path (fast fields open via `index_memory_segment`), so ordinary scans that snapshot the mutable segment should be able to hit the same assertion.
- Observed 104 times in one 60-minute Antithesis run (stressgres suites, fault injection including container kills of the postgres pod), pg_search main, PostgreSQL 18. Discovered by the index-consistency check added in #5915.

labels.name: antithesis
labels.description: Add this label to a PR to run all the Antithesis tests. Automatically removed.

comments: Thank you for reporting!

confirmed this. and its the same family as #3618 but in the other direction. just got done putting up #5955 for it

a mutable segment's header (`max_doc`, `num_deleted_docs` in `segment_metas`) and its `Add`/`Remove` list (its own blocks) are two separate WAL records with nothing atomic across them. `num_deleted_docs` is cumulative across deletes, and nothing ties a header value to a list length. on single node crash recovery, replay stops at some prefix boundary; if that lands between two paired writes, the header reflects a later op's counters while the list only has a prefix

[block.rs#L509-L520](https://github.com/paradedb/paradedb/blob/3e803a4f87bbcbdfb87190e920766a03d3c0464b/pg_search/src/postgres/storage/block.rs#L509-L520) uses the header as the source of truth for both the replay length and the expected count, while the list is the real length, so they disagree and the `assert_eq!` panics. header `(max_doc=20, num_deleted_docs=18)` with the 18 `Remove` entries missing gives your exact `left: 20 / right: 2`. its not replication (the custom rmgr refuses standby replay in the community build) and it clears on its own because a background merge rewrites the segment into an immutable one, not because the bytes heal

what shipped:
- now: swap the `assert_eq!` in `mutable_snapshot` for an early `Err` when the counts disagree, so the read fails cleanly and the next query (after the merge) succeeds. the read path already does `map_err(...)?`; the vacuum caller in delete.rs also needed to handle it or the panic just moves there. no `dst::assert_always!` alongside after all: in debug builds it lowers to a live `debug_assert!` that fires on exactly the torn path before the `Err`, and "always" is the wrong signal since this mismatch is expected after recovery
- follow-up: record a per-list length/generation in the header, written in the same record as the counters, so the snapshot replays to a known length. one record atomicity of the two writes isnt doable (generic xlog caps at 4 buffers, the list append spans many blocks)
evidence: Mutable segment snapshot assertion fails after crash recovery: ctid_set.len() != expected_ctids

title: Window aggregates ignore solve_mvcc=true when top-k is unordered
body:
## Summary

`pdb.agg(..., solve_mvcc => true) OVER ()` (facet / window aggregate alongside top-k) silently ignores `solve_mvcc` when the query's top-k is **unordered** (no pushed-down ORDER BY). The aggregation then runs over raw index entries, including deleted-but-unvacuumed rows. The same request with a pushed-down ORDER BY is filtered correctly, so the identical `pdb.agg` call returns different answers depending on whether the query has an ORDER BY.

## Reproduction

```sql
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_search;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS mvcc_facet;
CREATE TABLE mvcc_facet (
    id serial8,
    val uuid NOT NULL
) WITH (autovacuum_enabled = off);

INSERT INTO mvcc_facet (val)
SELECT md5('facettest' || ((x % 12) + 1))::uuid
FROM generate_series(1, 1000000) x;

CREATE INDEX idx_mvcc_facet ON mvcc_facet
USING bm25 (id, val) WITH (key_field = 'id');

-- create unvacuumed dead rows
DELETE FROM mvcc_facet WHERE id % 10 = 0;      -- 100,000 rows
SELECT count(*) FROM mvcc_facet;               -- 900,000 live

-- ordered top-k facet: solve_mvcc=true honored
SELECT id, pdb.agg('{"value_count":{"field":"id"}}', true) OVER () AS agg
FROM mvcc_facet WHERE mvcc_facet @@@ pdb.all()
ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1;
--> {"value": 900000.0}   ✓

-- unordered top-k facet: same solve_mvcc=true request, no ORDER BY
SELECT id, pdb.agg('{"value_count":{"field":"id"}}', true) OVER () AS agg
FROM mvcc_facet WHERE mvcc_facet @@@ pdb.all()
LIMIT 1;
--> {"value": 1000000.0}  ✗ includes all 100,000 deleted rows
```

## Cause

In `pg_search/src/postgres/customscan/basescan/exec_methods/top_k.rs`, window-aggregate execution has two branches:

- **Ordered top-k** (`orderby_info.is_some()`): the aggregation collector is wrapped in `TopKAuxiliaryCollector` with a `VisibilityChecker`, so `mvcc_enabled` is honored.
- **Unordered top-k** (the `// Unordered TopK: run a standalone aggregation query` branch): the aggregation runs as a standalone `DistributedAggregationCollector` search with no visibility filtering at all. `prepare_aggregations` computes `mvcc_enabled` from the `pdb.agg` argument, but this branch never consults it.

## Notes

- On branch `cardinality-lazy-vischeck`, the lazy-eligible case (cardinality-only aggregations over string fields) attaches the lazy doc-visibility filter in this branch, so those specific facets are now correct. All other aggregate types (`value_count`, `avg`, `sum`, `terms`, numeric cardinality, ...) remain unfiltered in the unordered branch.
- Fix direction: apply the same visibility filtering as the ordered branch (e.g. an `MVCCFilterCollector`-style wrapper around the standalone aggregation search), plus a regression test with an unordered facet query over unvacuumed deletes so the two branches can't diverge again.

title: Query latency grows linearly with bytes buffered in mutable segments
body:
### What happens?

On a table whose BM25-indexed columns carry large text values (~100KB
parsed PDFs), single-row UPDATE commits degrade *every* query on the index
linearly — including queries matching zero rows. Measured ~70ms of added
query latency per MB of freshly committed indexed text (6.4M-doc corpus,
~1GB index):

| after N single-row ~120KB commits | zero-match query |
|---|---|
| 0 | 5–16 ms |
| 100 | ~700 ms |
| 500 | ~3.6 s |
| 1000 | ~8.4 s |

- `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`: all time inside the ParadeDB Base Scan,
  0 rows, 0 heap fetches, buffer hits proportional to buffered bytes,
  and the read query *dirties* buffers.
- `paradedb.index_info()` looks healthy throughout (segment count stable,
  0 deleted docs) — the cost is invisible to it.
- Batching the writes (100 rows/commit, same total bytes) does not help —
  the cost tracks bytes, not commits.
- VACUUM does not drain it.
- On 0.25.x, idle time heals it (background merging drains the buffer);
  under sustained writes the backlog is steady-state. On 0.24.1 it does
  not recover without REINDEX.
- `SET paradedb.global_mutable_segment_rows = 0` eliminates the problem
  completely (same churn stays ~2ms), confirming the mutable-segment
  buffer as the mechanism. The buffer appears to be capped by row count
  only; with large documents the byte volume is unbounded.

Real-world impact: our production instance (Dutch parliament documents,
continuous ingest of parsed PDF text) sat at a flat ~2.6s for every
search query, at any match count, recovering only briefly after a nightly
REINDEX.

### To Reproduce

```bash
docker run -d --name pdb -e POSTGRES_USER=t -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=t \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=t paradedb/paradedb:0.25.2-pg18
```

```sql
CREATE TABLE entries (
  id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
  search_text text,
  resource_search_text text,
  deleted boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false
);
INSERT INTO entries
SELECT g, 'onderwerp'||(g%50000)||' '||md5(g::text),
       CASE WHEN g%3=0 THEN 'verslag '||md5((g*7)::text) END, false
FROM generate_series(1, 6400000) g;

CREATE INDEX ix ON entries USING bm25 (id,
  ((search_text)::pdb.simple('stemmer=Dutch', 'ascii_folding=true')),
  ((resource_search_text)::pdb.simple('stemmer=Dutch', 'ascii_folding=true')))
WITH (key_field=id) WHERE deleted IS FALSE;
```

Baseline (fast):

```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT id, pdb.score(id) AS s FROM entries
WHERE (search_text @@@ pdb.match('xyzzyqplonk')
       OR resource_search_text @@@ pdb.match('xyzzyqplonk'))
  AND deleted IS FALSE
ORDER BY s DESC LIMIT 21;
```

Churn (in a shell — separate transactions matter less than total bytes):

```bash
for k in $(seq 1 1000); do
  psql -U t -d t -q -c "UPDATE entries SET resource_search_text =
    (SELECT string_agg(md5(g::text || clock_timestamp()::text), ' ')
     FROM generate_series(1,3600) g)
   WHERE id = (SELECT (random()*6400000)::bigint + 1);"
done
```

Re-run the query: multi-second. `SET paradedb.global_mutable_segment_rows
= 0` + REINDEX and repeat the churn: stays ~2ms.

### OS:

macOS arm64 + Debian x86

### ParadeDB Version (e.g. output of `SELECT * FROM paradedb.version_info();`):

0.24.1-pg18, 0.25.1-pg17, 0.25.1-pg18, 0.25.2-pg18

title: [Bug] K8s环境下 Nacos 1.4.8 无法剔除已下线的Pod实例（僵尸实例/脏数据）
body: 问题描述： 在 K8s 生产环境中使用 Nacos 1.4.8 集群（AP模式）时，我们遇到了一个严重的问题： 当后端的 Java 业务 Pod 被销毁或重建后，旧的 Pod IP（实际上已经物理销毁并停止了心跳）依然残留在 Nacos 控制台的服务列表中，并且健康状态（healthy）依然显示为 true。 我们的业务网关（Spring Cloud Gateway）拉取到了这个已经失效的“僵尸 IP”，并持续将流量转发给它，导致线上出现大量 connection timed out 请求超时报错。 我们排查了 K8s 集群底层，确认该 Pod 确实早已下线并彻底销毁。直到我们手动重启了 Nacos 集群节点后，Nacos 内存里的脏数据才被清空，僵尸 IP 消失，服务列表恢复正常。怀疑是 1.4.x 版本在 K8s 动态网络下，集群节点间状态同步（Distro 协议）存在缺陷导致脏数据无法被清理。 预期行为： 当 K8s 中的 Pod 销毁并停止向 Nacos 发送心跳后，Nacos 应当在 30 秒超时后自动、彻底地将该实例从注册表中剔除，即使集群节点间存在网络微小抖动，也不应出现死实例长期假在线的情况。 实际行为： 已经死掉的实例永远挂在 Nacos 注册中心里，健康状态持续显示为 true，服务剔除机制针对该实例完全失效。只能通过重启整个 Nacos 集群来清理脏数据。 问题可能复现流程： 1、在 K8s 环境（使用 Calico CNI）中部署 Nacos 1.4.8 集群版。 2、将后端的 Spring Cloud 应用注册到该 Nacos 集群。 3、在 K8s 中对应用 Pod 进行强制删除或滚动更新。 4、观察 Nacos 控制台，有概率会出现旧 Pod IP 长期残留且不被自动剔除。 环境信息： Kubernetes (Calico CNI 网络插件) Nacos-server 1.4.8（集群模式） Client: Spring Cloud Alibaba（Java） 报错如下： 图片说明：由于特殊原因图片需要打码，然后上面圈出来的Pod IP地址是业务后端的IP地址，图片中的日志是网关服务的日志，转发给业务后端IP地址获取的和上面真实的IP地址不一致。

关于你说的问题，简单回答一下：

可能性有2：

1. 出现幽灵pod， pod看起来销毁了，但是进程在node中还在运行，主动上报心跳，nacos认为实例还健康，因此未移除。
2. 节点之间的网络存在问题或配置存在问题，导致nacos的distro协议在进行责任节点处理时未正确计算责任节点，未及时删除。

排查方向：
1. 开启naming-event.log的debug模式， 确认心跳是否还在发送
2. 检查节点之间的cluster.conf文件，以及nacos-cluster.log中的healhty server list是否有变化，以及是否和实际节点一致。
3. naming-distro.log， protocol-distro.log， naming-server.log 查看对应服务信息，是否有报错等。

title: Skill draft update leaves deleted resource files in storage
body:
**Describe the bug**

Updating an existing Skill draft with a reduced resource-file set updates the version storage descriptor but does not delete the omitted files from the configured AI storage provider. The omitted files become unreferenced storage objects and cannot be cleaned by later draft or Skill deletion.

**Expected behavior**

A Skill draft update is a full-content replacement. After the update succeeds, files that were referenced by the previous storage descriptor but are absent from the new Skill content should be deleted through the provider persisted for that version.

**Actually behavior**

`SkillOperationServiceImpl.updateDraft` calls `writeSkillToStorage` for the new content and replaces the version storage descriptor with the returned file list. `writeSkillToStorage` only saves files present in the request. It does not compare the old and new file lists or delete removed files.

The removed files disappear from Skill query/download results because the new descriptor no longer references them, but their backing storage entries remain. Later deletion reads only the new descriptor, so those entries remain orphaned.

**How to Reproduce**

1. Create a Skill draft containing `SKILL.md` and multiple resource files.
2. Update the same draft while omitting one or more existing resource files.
3. Query or download the draft and confirm that the omitted files are no longer returned.
4. Inspect the configured AI storage provider and observe that the omitted file entries still exist.
5. Delete the draft or Skill and observe that the orphaned entries are not cleaned because they are absent from the current storage descriptor.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: All
- Version: current `develop`
- Module: `ai`
- SDK: original

**Additional context**

The fix should preserve the version's persisted storage provider, compare the previous and replacement descriptors, and delete only the removed file keys. The Skill specification should also clarify that draft overwrite/update replaces the complete package content and removes omitted resource files from storage.

title: nacos-client 3.2.3: sun.misc.Unsafe::allocateMemory warning from shaded Netty still reproduces on JDK 25
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #14070 — the `sun.misc.Unsafe` terminally-deprecated warning from nacos-client is still present with the latest version on JDK 25.

As suggested by the maintainer in #14070 ("grpc already upgrade in 3.1.2, please retry in new version and if problem still exist, please submit new issue and link to this issue"), I retried with **nacos-client 3.2.3** (newer than 3.1.2) and the warning still reproduces on every startup.

## Warning log

```
WARNING: A terminally deprecated method in sun.misc.Unsafe has been called
WARNING: sun.misc.Unsafe::allocateMemory has been called by com.alibaba.nacos.shaded.io.grpc.netty.shaded.io.netty.util.internal.PlatformDependent0$2 (file:/D:/maven/resp/com/alibaba/nacos/nacos-client/3.2.3/nacos-client-3.2.3.jar)
WARNING: Please consider reporting this to the maintainers of class com.alibaba.nacos.shaded.io.grpc.netty.shaded.io.netty.util.internal.PlatformDependent0$2
WARNING: sun.misc.Unsafe::allocateMemory will be removed in a future release
```

## Environment

- JDK: 25 (25.0.2)
- nacos-client: 3.2.3
- Spring Boot: 4.0.x

## Analysis

The warning is triggered by the **shaded Netty** `PlatformDependent0` (off-heap allocation path via `Unsafe::allocateMemory`). Since the call comes from Netty's off-heap allocation logic, upgrading grpc/netty alone does not seem to remove the call itself.

Another user also confirmed the same problem in #14070 (comment by yangyuanqiang, 2026-08-13).

## Questions

1. Is there any plan to address this in a future nacos-client release (e.g. bumping the shaded Netty to a version that no longer calls `Unsafe::allocateMemory`, or starting with `--sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access=allow` by default)?
2. For now, is `--sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access=allow` the only workaround for JDK 25 users?

Related: #14070

title: Role search returns no result when the username filter contains an underscore
body:
## Describe the bug

On a standalone Nacos server (embedded Derby storage, the default), searching roles with **both** the username filter and the role filter returns no result as soon as the username contains an underscore. Filtering by only one of the two works.

## Expected behavior

`_` is a literal character in a username, so searching `na_cos` should return the matching role rows, exactly as it does when the role filter is left empty.

## Actual behavior

The query returns zero rows.

## How to reproduce

1. Start Nacos in standalone mode (embedded Derby) with auth enabled.
2. Create a user `na_cos` and bind it to a role `ro_le`.
3. Open Console -> Permissions -> Roles.
4. Search with username `na_cos` **and** role `ro_le` -> no result.
5. Search with username `na_cos` only -> the row is returned.

## Root cause

`EmbeddedRolePersistServiceImpl#findRolesLike4Page` appends the escape clause once, after both `LIKE` predicates have been built:

```java
if (StringUtils.isNotBlank(username)) {
    where.append(" AND username LIKE ? ");
    params.add(generateLikeArgument(username));
}
if (StringUtils.isNotBlank(role)) {
    where.append(" AND role LIKE ? ");
    params.add(generateLikeArgument(role));
}
if (CollectionUtils.isNotEmpty(params)) {
    where.append(SQL_DERBY_ESCAPE_BACK_SLASH_FOR_LIKE);
}
```

which produces:

```sql
WHERE 1 = 1  AND username LIKE ?  AND role LIKE ?  ESCAPE '\'
```

In SQL, `ESCAPE` qualifies only the single `LIKE` predicate it immediately follows. The clause therefore applies to `role` alone, and the `username` predicate is left without one. Since `generateLikeArgument` has already rewritten `_` into `\_`, Derby matches the backslash literally and the predicate can never be satisfied.

When only one filter is set the single predicate happens to be the last one, so the clause lands correctly. That is why the defect only shows up when both filters are combined.

## Evidence

Executed against Derby 10.14.2.0 with rows `('na_cos', 'ro_le')` and `('naXcos', 'roXle')`, binding `%na\_cos%` and `%ro\_le%`:

| SQL | Result |
|-----|--------|
| `... AND username LIKE ? AND role LIKE ? ESCAPE '\'` | `rows=0` |
| `... AND username LIKE ? ESCAPE '\' AND role LIKE ? ESCAPE '\'` | `rows=1` (`na_cos/ro_le`) |

## Scope

Only `findRolesLike4Page` combines two fuzzy predicates. The user and permission searches in the same module build a single `LIKE` predicate each and already place the clause correctly, so they are unaffected.

## Environment

- Version: `develop` (3.3.0-SNAPSHOT)
- Module: auth (`plugin-default-impl/nacos-default-auth-plugin`)
- Storage: embedded (Derby)

title: Recursive custom syntax definition can crash MacOS due to OOM
body:
Hello, I was trying to make bat highlight files with `uv run` shebangs and an agent wrote a recursive syntax definition that crashes MacOS due to unbounded memory consumption. I thought you'd probably want to protect against this here or in syntect.

**What steps will reproduce the bug?**

The agent wrote this:

```yaml
DON'T ACTUALLY USE THIS

  %YAML 1.2
  ---
  name: Python (uv script)
  file_extensions: []
  scope: source.python
  first_line_match: '^#!.*\buv\s+run\b.*--script\b'
  contexts:
    main:
      - include: scope:source.python

```



<details>

  <summary>Here's an agent-written repro
  </summary>

# A custom syntax whose `scope:` collides with the syntax it `include`s causes unbounded memory allocation (kernel panic)

⚠️ **Do not run the repro below unsandboxed.** On my machine `bat` allocated ~6 GB/s and twice took down the whole OS (macOS watchdog kernel panic, 48 GB RAM). The repro as written is bounded with `timeout`.

## Summary

If a custom `.sublime-syntax` declares a `scope:` that is the same as the scope it pulls in via `include: scope:...`, the include resolves to the syntax itself. `bat cache --build` accepts this without complaint, and then highlighting *any* file that maps to that syntax allocates without bound until the machine dies. No output is ever produced.

I hit this accidentally — the offending 8-line syntax file was written by an LLM agent trying to add `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script` shebang detection, and it took my laptop down twice before I found it. A malformed syntax definition shouldn't be able to do that.

## Versions

- `bat` 0.26.1 (Homebrew bottle), which vendors `syntect` 5.3.0
- macOS 26.6 (25G72), arm64 (M5 Pro, 48 GB)

## Repro

```sh
R=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$R/config/syntaxes" "$R/cache"

cat > "$R/config/syntaxes/loop.sublime-syntax" <<'YAML'
%YAML 1.2
---
name: Loopy Python
file_extensions: [loopy]
scope: source.python              # <-- same scope as the bundled Python syntax
contexts:
  main:
    - include: scope:source.python  # <-- therefore resolves to *this* syntax
YAML

bat cache --build --source "$R/config" --target "$R/cache"   # succeeds, no warning

printf 'x = 1\n' > "$R/t.loopy"

# BOUNDED: kill after 2s. Without the timeout this eats all RAM.
BAT_CACHE_PATH="$R/cache" timeout 2 bat --color=always --paging=never "$R/t.loopy"
```

Sampling RSS of the `bat` process during those 2 seconds on a one-line input file:

```
t=250ms:    10 MB
t=500ms:  2388 MB
t=750ms:  3988 MB
t=1000ms: 5568 MB
t=1250ms: 7118 MB
```

It never emits the highlighted line. Left alone it reached 26.7 GB and 41.1 GB resident in two separate incidents before the kernel watchdog panicked (`Compressor Info: 100% of compressed pages limit (BAD)`), taking the machine down.

## Control

Changing only the `scope:` line so the include is no longer self-referential makes it work correctly and instantly:

```yaml
scope: source.python.uv
contexts:
  main:
    - include: scope:source.python
```

## Expected

`bat cache --build` should reject (or at minimum warn about) a syntax whose context graph reaches itself through `include: scope:`, rather than producing a cache that makes `bat` unrunnable on the affected file types. Failing that, the highlighter should bail out with an error instead of allocating without bound.

Note that `syntect` 5.3.0 already contains a fix for [#597](https://github.com/trishume/syntect/issues/597) ("infinite loop when a syntax definition continually pushes contexts without consuming any input"), so this appears to be a distinct case that the existing guard doesn't cover.


</details>


**What happens?**
OOMs MacOS


**What did you expect to happen instead?**
Something less dramatic


**How did you install `bat`?**
homebrew

title: Support `-v`, `-e`, and `-t` for `cat` compatibility
body:
## What would you like to see?

Add cat-compatible `-v`, `-e`, and `-t` options.

Expected behavior:

- `-v` / `--show-nonprinting` uses caret and `M-` notation for nonprinting bytes, except tabs and line feeds.
- `-e` includes `-v` behavior and writes `$` before each line feed.
- `-t` includes `-v` behavior and writes tabs as `^I`.
- Support files, standard input, multiple inputs, combined short options, and piped output.

These are grouped in one issue because `-e` and `-t` both include `-v`'s nonprinting behavior.

For example:

```console
$ printf 'a\tb\r\007\n' | bat -t
a^Ib^M^G
```

## Why?

Commands written for cat currently fail when `cat` is replaced interactively with bat:

```console
$ printf 'a\tb\n' | bat -v
error: unexpected argument '-v' found
```

I use `cat=bat` in an interactive shell, where commands copied from documentation or produced by shell tooling and agents can hit this incompatibility.

The missing options are noted in [#134](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/issues/134#issuecomment-2160884143). [#1749](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/issues/1749) was closed and discussed `-v` isn't a POSIX `cat` option (unlcear if that was exact reason for closure since it veered into discussion of -A flag).

Bat does implement selected non-POSIX `cat` options, including `-n`, `-s` ([#2665](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/pull/2665)), and `-b` ([#3857](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat/pull/3857)); the latter two were added after #1749. This request wouldn't change default output or behavior for POSIX invocations.

Since #1749, bat has added a reusable caret renderer and expanded it to every ASCII control character plus DEL (#2443, #2712). This provides part of the machinery needed for -v, although tab and line-feed handling and GNU/uutils M- notation still require new work.

## Implementation considerations

The options can share a mode controlling nonprinting bytes, line endings, and tabs. Bat's caret renderer already handles every ASCII control character, but compatibility still requires selectively preserving spaces, tabs, and line feeds and using GNU/uutils `M-` output for high-bit bytes instead of Unicode or hexadecimal escaping.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- `bat -t` writes tabs as `^I` without adding end-of-line markers.
- The options work with files, standard input, multiple inputs, combined short options, and piped output.
- Existing binary handling, styling, decorations, and default output remain unchanged.

title: Feature request: dedicated trim mode (ripple/roll/slip/slide) for the Studio timeline
body:
Studio's current timeline trim (drag a clip edge) only changes that one clip's in/out — it doesn't ripple neighboring clips, and there's no dedicated mode comparable to Final Cut Pro's Precision Editor (two-up in/out view, ripple/roll/slip/slide as distinct operations).

For anyone doing real multi-clip re-editing (not just nudging one element), the lack of ripple support means every trim risks creating overlaps or gaps that have to be manually closed by hand — there's no single action that trims one clip and shifts the rest of the track to match.

Would love to see:
- A roll edit (adjust the shared edit point between two adjacent clips, extending one and shortening the other by the same amount)
- A ripple trim (trim one clip, automatically shift everything after it on that track)
- Optionally, an FCP-style precision/trim view showing both sides of a cut at once

Happy to give more detail on the use case if useful.

title: Global skill mirroring should avoid redundant agent directories and provide target controls
body:
## Summary

Pi natively discovers global skills from both [`~/.pi/agent/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/skills.md#locations).

When a HyperFrames skill update performs an install, HyperFrames writes the selected skill bundles to Claude Code's global store and the universal `~/.agents/skills` store. It then mirrors **all globally installed HyperFrames skills attributed to its source** into detected agent-specific directories. Because Pi is in that mirror table, HyperFrames creates matching entries under `~/.pi/agent/skills` even though Pi already loads the universal copies.

Pi consequently discovers each mirrored skill twice, reports a name collision, keeps the `~/.pi/agent/skills` entry, and skips the `~/.agents/skills` entry.

**Clarification about `.claude`:** Pi does not load `~/.claude/skills` by default. That path appears here only because HyperFrames currently uses Claude Code's global skill store as the source for its fan-out. On Unix, the redundant Pi entries are symlinks back to that source. The two locations Pi actually discovers in this reproduction are `~/.pi/agent/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`.

This is deterministic duplicate discovery, not the unrelated-skill deletion reported in #3111. It is also narrower than the silent-update and overwrite concerns in #2613.

## Environment

- HyperFrames CLI `0.7.109`
- Pi `0.84.2`
- macOS
- Default `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (therefore Claude's store is `~/.claude/skills`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have Pi installed, so `~/.pi/agent/` exists.
2. Have HyperFrames skills installed globally, including copies under `~/.agents/skills`.
3. Remove or otherwise ensure the matching HyperFrames entries are absent from `~/.pi/agent/skills`.
4. Make at least one HyperFrames skill stale or missing so the next update performs an install rather than a no-op.
5. Run:

   ```sh
   npx hyperframes skills update product-launch-video
   ```

6. Observe output similar to:

   ```text
   Linked skills into 12 other agent directories.
   ```

7. Inspect the Pi directory. With the default Claude configuration, entries look like:

   ```text
   ~/.pi/agent/skills/hyperframes -> ../../../.claude/skills/hyperframes
   ```

8. Start Pi. It reports collisions such as:

   ```text
   "hyperframes" collision:
     ✓ auto (user) ~/.pi/agent/skills/hyperframes/SKILL.md
     ✗ ~/.agents/skills/hyperframes/SKILL.md (skipped)
   ```

In the observed reproduction, HyperFrames created 12 Pi symlinks and all 12 corresponding `SKILL.md` files were byte-identical to the universal copies. They still collide because Pi discovers them through two configured locations.

## Root cause in the current implementation

- `packages/cli/src/commands/skills.ts` invokes the upstream installer globally with `--agent claude-code universal --copy`.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/skillsMirror.ts` then chooses Claude's global store (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills`, defaulting to `~/.claude/skills`) as the fan-out source.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/agentDirs.generated.ts` includes Pi at `.pi/agent/skills`.
- The mirror skips the Claude source and `~/.agents/skills` themselves, but Pi's agent-specific path is different, so it is mirrored despite Pi already consuming the universal store.
- The fan-out runs after an actual install. A freshness check that is a complete no-op does not recreate the links.

On Unix the fan-out uses relative symlinks; on Windows it copies directories. Either form can create duplicate Pi discovery when the universal copy is also present.

## Expected behavior

HyperFrames should not create multiple discoverable copies of the same skill for one agent by default.

A defensible design would provide:

1. **Capability-aware `auto` behavior by default** — do not mirror into an agent-specific directory when that agent already consumes the universal store.
2. **A persistent opt-out** — users should be able to disable global fan-out entirely.
3. **Optional target controls** — advanced users should be able to include or exclude specific agents.
4. **Non-interactive determinism** — agent-triggered updates should honor saved or default behavior without prompting on every run.

Possible CLI shapes, offered only as examples:

```sh
hyperframes skills update --no-mirror
hyperframes skills update --mirror-agents cursor,goose
```

The exact interface is open for maintainers to choose. A Pi-specific exclusion would fix this reproduction. A broader target-control design would also support users who deliberately manage several agent skill stores differently.

If explicit Pi mirroring is supported, the install targets must be coordinated: installing the same skill names into both Pi's agent-specific directory and `~/.agents/skills` preserves the collision.

## Acceptance criteria

- The default update path does not create Pi skill collisions when the same HyperFrames skills are installed under `~/.agents/skills`.
- Users have a documented way to prevent or scope mirroring without patching generated files or an npm cache.
- Existing non-redundant agent mirroring continues to work.
- A regression test covers an installed Pi plus the universal store.
evidence: Global skill mirroring should avoid redundant agent directories and provide target controls
## Environment - HyperFrames CLI `0.7.109` - Pi `0.84.2` - macOS - Default `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (therefore Claude's store is `~/.claude/skills`) ## Steps to reproduce 1.

title: Evaluate transaction based pooling
body:
As a system administrator, I want Zammad to support transaction-based connection pooling for PostgreSQL (in addition to session-based pooling) so that I can reduce the number of database connections required to run Zammad, especially in larger or high-concurrency deployments.

## Acceptance criteria

- Research and document whether Rails (and the specific Rails version used by Zammad) can operate with transaction-based pooling (e.g. via PgBouncer in transaction mode) without breaking functionality
  - Pay particular attention to features that rely on session state, such as prepared statements, advisory locks, `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY`, and temporary tables
- Identify which parts of Zammad's codebase (if any) rely on session-level PostgreSQL features that would be incompatible with transaction-based pooling
- Produce a recommendation on whether transaction-based pooling can be supported, and if so, under which conditions or with which limitations
- Document the findings in a way that can be used to decide on a follow-up implementation ticket, if applicable

## Background information

Zammad currently relies on session-based connection pooling for PostgreSQL, which is the traditional and default approach for Rails applications. As deployments grow in size and concurrency, session-based pooling can become a bottleneck due to the higher number of persistent database connections required. Transaction-based pooling (e.g. via PgBouncer) can significantly reduce the number of open connections, but it also imposes restrictions on the use of session-level PostgreSQL features. This spike aims to challenge the assumption that Zammad must use session-based pooling, and to determine whether a switch to (or additional support for) transaction-based pooling is technically feasible.

title: 🐛 [Mixpost] connect() to unix:/var/run/php/php8.2-fpm.sock failed (2: No such file or directory) while connecting to upstream
body:
### Store Application

Mixpost

### App version

2.1.3

### Description

We encountered an issue while running Mixpost on a Docker container in Runtipi. The Nginx error logs showed repeated failures to connect to PHP-FPM via the socket:

```pgsql
connect() to unix:/var/run/php/php8.2-fpm.sock failed (2: No such file or directory) while connecting to upstream
```

### Root Cause
The installed PHP version was 8.3, but Nginx was configured to use the PHP 8.2 socket (php8.2-fpm.sock), which did not exist.
Additionally, the /etc/nginx/conf.d/ directory was empty, meaning there was no active Nginx configuration for handling PHP requests.

### Solution
1. Checked existing configuration files

No valid site configuration was found in /etc/nginx/conf.d/.
2. Created a new Nginx configuration

A new config file /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf was created with the correct PHP-FPM socket reference (php8.3-fpm.sock):
```nginx
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name localhost;
    root /var/www/html/public;
    index index.php index.html index.htm;

    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$query_string;
    }

    location ~ \.php$ {
        include fastcgi_params;
        fastcgi_pass unix:/var/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock;
        fastcgi_index index.php;
        fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $document_root$fastcgi_script_name;
    }
}
```
3. Restarted services

Restarted PHP-FPM and Nginx to apply the changes:
```bash
service php8.3-fpm restart
service nginx restart
```

### Conclusion
The issue was caused by an incorrect PHP-FPM socket reference and a missing Nginx configuration. Updating the Nginx config and ensuring the correct PHP version resolved the problem. This should be addressed in Runtipi’s setup scripts to ensure compatibility with the installed PHP version.

comments:
Hello @innocentius,

Thanks for reporting this.
Apparently the app changed name from **LobeChat** to **LobeHub** so the dependency bot couldn't see the [v2 release](https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/releases/tag/v2.0.0).

From what I see our initial implementation was pretty minimal install with no persistent data, so this would probably deserve a new app.
I will need time to look into this.

Hello! @Lancelot-Enguerrand ,

Appreciate your fast response, and thank you for explaining the reason behind this!

To be perfectly fair, Lobechat has become pretty much a mess through the constant updates -- in fact I would prefer to not update it if I have the choice. The reason why I asked in the first place is because of an annoying bug in the current version. The app now displays an ad about the Lobechat's own deepseek service every time it starts. Not only that, because of some other bug, the app would quit and reload, which lose all progress while displaying the ad again. 

I'm also aware that runtipi official store is currently not accepting new apps. Personally I have tried to self-host Lobechat (with knowledge database setup), but I also find it convoluted. I think most people will be okay with a minimal install to the latest version. If you would bless us with a persistent data installation, that would be great.

title: Auto-restore gameinfo.gi to vanila on game exit
body:
## Summary

Feature request: opt-in toggle to automatically restore gameinfo.gi to vanilla state when Deadlock process closes.

### Basic example

Currently, if I launch modded and then want to play via Steam without mods, I have to launch DMM and manually click "Reset to Vanilla" or choose clean profile. 
It would be great if there was opt-in toggle to allow the mod manager to detect when the game process has closed and automatically reset gameinfo.gi back to the original state.

### Motivation

This would allow users to:

- Launch modded via the mod manager when they want mods

- Launch via Steam normally and always get a clean vanilla game without launching DMM

title: Default download routing has no fallback when a cache node is unreachable
body:
Split out of a discussion on #565 (https://github.com/deadlock-mod-manager/deadlock-mod-manager/pull/565#issuecomment-5112638418), where it was out of scope.

## Problem

A download request goes to whichever GameBanana cache host the API handed out, and the downloader has no way to try another one. When that specific host is unreachable (as opposed to the transfer failing) every download fails and there is nothing the app or the user can do about it. Retrying, including the new retry button in #565, re-requests the same URL and fails the same way.

There is currently no fallback anywhere in the download path. The only `mirror` reference in the desktop source is an unrelated SVG prop.

## What this looked like in practice

Every mod I tried failed identically:

```
[03:13:37] Download failed for mod 650634: Network error: Failed to send request:
           error sending request for url (https://filecache44.gamebanana.com/mods/qollock_319_13july.zip)
[03:18:19] Download failed for mod 695042: Network error: Failed to send request:
           error sending request for url (https://filecache44.gamebanana.com/mods/raven-cane.zip)
```

Both after exactly 30 s, matching `connect_timeout` at `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/download_manager/downloader.rs:193`. `error sending request` is a connection-level failure, it never got as far as an HTTP status.

`filecache44.gamebanana.com` (209.222.101.8, ReliableSite) was unroutable from my ISP. TCP 443 and 80 both blackholed, and `traceroute` died inside the ISP without the packets ever leaving it:

```
 6  187.100.42.71  9.256 ms
 7  * * *      (through hop 18)
```

Sibling hosts over the same link were fine: `filecache43` (185.150.191.106), `filecache45` (104.243.32.234) and `images.gamebanana.com` all accepted connections, and a traceroute to `filecache43` left the ISP normally at hop 8. GameBanana's own `/fileservers` page reported 44 as up, which it presumably was from their vantage point.

So this is not a GameBanana outage and not an app bug, the app is accurately reporting a network failure. But the result is that the app is unusable for downloads while being one hostname away from working, and it has no way to route around it.

## Possible directions

Not a proposal, just the options as I see them:

1. **Client-side retry against a sibling host.** On a connect-level failure (as distinct from a 4xx/5xx or a mid-transfer error), rewrite the host to another `filecacheNN` and retry once or twice. Cheapest to implement; assumes the same path exists on other nodes, which I didn't verify.
2. **Have the API return more than one candidate URL.** The desktop app already gets download metadata from `api.deadlockmods.app`; that payload could carry alternates and let the client fall through. More robust, more work, and a schema change.
3. **Route through the mirror service.** `apps/mirror-service` already exists, I don't know whether it is intended to cover this case.

Option 1 alone would have turned a total outage into a transparent recovery in my case.

## Adjacent, smaller

The failure surfaces as a generic download error. Distinguishing "could not reach the file server" from "the download failed" would at least tell a user this is not their fault and not something a retry will resolve.

### Environment

- OS: Fedora 44, KDE / Wayland
- Flatpak build (CEF)

Correction to the original report: **I was wrong that there is no fallback in the download path.** There is one, and I missed it.

`apps/desktop/src/lib/download/fileserver.ts` implements `resolveDownloadFileUrls`, `manager.ts:337` calls `getGameBananaFileservers()`, and Settings has a "Download routing" section (`FileserverSettings`) offering `default` / `auto` / pin-a-specific-server, with a latency test per server. `auto` picks the lowest-latency server that is up, which is exactly the mechanism I said was missing. Apologies for the noise.

The gap is narrower than I described, but I think something is still here:

1. **`default` is the default, and it does no fallback.** `resolveDownloadFileUrls` returns the files untouched when `preference === "default"` (`fileserver.ts:104`), so an out-of-the-box install has no protection.
2. **A connect-level failure does not trigger a re-route or point at the setting.** After 9 files failed against a dead node, nothing suggested that "Download routing" exists. Switching to `auto` on a connect failure (or even just surfacing the setting in the error) would close the loop without the user having to know the feature is there.
3. **The failing host is invisible in the error.** With `default`, the URL is `https://gamebanana.com/dl/<id>`, which redirects to a cache node. The failure surfaces against the original URL:

   ```
   Download failed for mod 650634: Network error: Failed to send request:
   error sending request for url (https://gamebanana.com/dl/1627686)
   ```

   `gamebanana.com` itself is reachable here since all three of its IPv4 addresses accept connections, so the 30 s failure is on the redirect target, not the URL named in the message. I have not captured the redirect to confirm which node it resolved to, so treat that last step as inference rather than measured.

Standing facts from the original report, re-verified since with the VPN disconnected (it was never involved, the destination was never routed through the tunnel): `filecache44.gamebanana.com` (209.222.101.8) still times out on TCP 443, while `filecache43` and `filecache45` connect fine over the same link.

title: Linux game launch cannot detect xdg-open failure and reports success regardless
body:
## Problem

On Linux, `SteamManager::launch_game` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/mod_manager/steam_manager.rs:186-199`) shells out to `xdg-open` and cannot tell whether it worked:

```rust
std::process::Command::new("xdg-open")
  .arg(&steam_uri)
  .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())
  .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null())
  .spawn()
  .map_err(|e| Error::GameLaunchFailed(e.to_string()))?;
```

`spawn()` succeeds as soon as the process is created, so the exit status is never observed, and both output streams are discarded. Any failure inside `xdg-open` is invisible to the app: it logs `Launching game with URI: …` and reports success while nothing launches.

The Windows branch of the same function already avoids this by invoking the Steam executable with the URI directly, and `get_steam_executable()` returns `steam.sh` on Linux but nothing uses it there.

## How I hit it

A `steam://run/…` launch silently did nothing from the app's perspective. The only visible error came from KDE, not the manager:

```
Could not read file steam://run/1422450//-condebug.
```

The underlying cause was environmental on my machine where a `~/.local/share/applications/steam.desktop` written by Plasma's "Edit Application…" dialog, shadowing the packaged entry with an empty `MimeType=`. KIO therefore found no handler for `x-scheme-handler/steam` and fell back to treating the URI as a file path. Fixing the desktop file resolved the launch.

That part is not a bug in this project. What is worth addressing is that the app had no idea any of it happened. With the exit status checked, it could have surfaced "Steam did not accept the launch request" instead of appearing to succeed.

## Why this is not just "call steam.sh like Windows does"

Under Flatpak, `xdg-open` is the right mechanism since it is the portal shim, and the host resolves the handler. Running the host's `steam.sh` from inside the sandbox would execute Steam in the container's namespace, even though `--filesystem=~/.local/share/Steam` makes the file reachable. Verified inside the installed Flatpak:

```
$ flatpak run --command=which dev.stormix.deadlock-mod-manager xdg-open
/usr/bin/xdg-open
```

So the environments want different things:

| Environment | Suggested |
|---|---|
| Windows | Steam executable + URI (already the case) |
| Linux, native | Steam executable + URI directly skips `xdg-open`, KIO, and desktop-file resolution entirely |
| Linux, Flatpak | keep `xdg-open` via the portal, or `flatpak-spawn --host steam <uri>` |

`is_flatpak()` already exists at `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/flatpak.rs:61` (`FLATPAK_ID` presence), and `flatpak-spawn --host` is already used by the updater at `flatpak.rs:113`, so both branches have precedent in the codebase.

Going direct on native Linux has a real benefit beyond error reporting: it is immune to a broken or shadowed `steam.desktop`, which is exactly what bit me and is entirely outside the user's awareness when it happens.

## Suggested scope

1. Capture the exit status rather than fire-and-forget, and stop discarding stderr so the reason reaches the log.
2. On native Linux, launch the Steam executable with the URI directly; keep the portal path under Flatpak.
3. Report a real error to the UI when the launch is rejected.

## Adjacent, probably its own issue

Deep-link registration fails inside the Flatpak because `xdg-mime` is not in the runtime:

```
[DeepLink] Failed to run OS command `xdg-mime`: No such file or directory (os error 2)
[DeepLink] Failed to register protocols: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

```
$ flatpak run --command=which dev.stormix.deadlock-mod-manager xdg-mime
which: no xdg-mime in (/app/bin:/usr/bin)
```

Same underlying theme, shelling out to xdg-utils and assuming it is present and working. Happy to split this out if you would rather track it separately.

### Environment

- OS: Fedora 44, KDE Plasma 6 / Wayland
- Reproduced on a native dev build; the Flatpak analysis above is from the installed CEF build

title: Importing large raw VPK (~200 MB) freezes/fails while compressed archive succeeds
body:
## Summary

Importing a large raw `.vpk` through drag-and-drop or upload files freezes and then fails, while importing the exact same VPK inside a compressed RAR archive succeeds.

The raw-file command currently reads the entire dropped file into a `Vec<u8>` and returns it through the Tauri command boundary:

https://github.com/deadlock-mod-manager/deadlock-mod-manager/blob/v1.1.0/apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/archive.rs

```rust
#[tauri::command]
pub async fn read_dropped_mod_file(file_path: String) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error> {
    let validated_path =
        crate::dropped_mod_file::validate_dropped_mod_file_path(&file_path)?;

    log::info!(
        "Reading dropped mod file from path: {}",
        validated_path.display()
    );

    tokio::fs::read(&validated_path).await.map_err(Error::from)
}
```

For a ~200 MB VPK, returning the complete buffer across the backend/frontend boundary appears to stall the import path.

## Environment

- Deadlock Mod Manager: 1.1.0
- Windows x64, build 26200
- Raw VPK size: 200,628,978 bytes
- Same VPK compressed as RAR: 33,794,669 bytes

## Reproduction

1. Drag a valid ~200 MB raw VPK into the Mod Manager.
2. The UI freezes and the import fails.
3. Restart the manager and repeat with another known-working ~199 MB raw VPK; it also fails.
4. Put the same 200 MB VPK inside a compressed RAR archive.
5. Drag the archive into the manager; extraction, VPK copying, hero detection, and installation complete successfully.

The raw VPK passes full VPK checksum verification in Source 2 Viewer and works when installed manually, so this is not archive corruption.

## Relevant log behavior

The raw import only logs the read operation twice, roughly 6–7 seconds apart, with no parsing error or successful continuation:

```text
Reading dropped mod file from path: ...\mod.vpk
Reading dropped mod file from path: ...\mod.vpk
```

The compressed archive proceeds through:

```text
Reading dropped mod file from path: ...\mod.rar
Extracting archive: ...
Successfully extracted RAR archive
Extracted 1 VPK files
Successfully copied 1 VPKs for local mod
```

## Expected behavior

Large valid raw VPKs should import without loading and serializing the whole file through the frontend command channel.

## Suggested fix

Keep local-file handling in Rust after path validation:

- pass/retain the validated path and copy/process the VPK from the backend; or
- stream/chunk the file instead of returning a full `Vec<u8>`.

If a full-buffer path must remain, detecting oversized files and displaying a useful error would be preferable to freezing and invoking the read again.

When commits are created through the agent workflow, the Git author/ownership metadata appears to always include Claude-related identity.

I would like commits to use only my own email by default:
- `agent@thomas.md`

By default, commits should use the repository/user-configured Git identity, and in my case that should be:
- Email: `agent@thomas.md`

Claude-related identity should not be injected unless explicitly enabled.

- Commit attribution is currently incorrect for my workflow.
- It creates noise in commit history and ownership.
- It makes automation/audit rules based on author email harder to maintain.

1. What is the precedence order currently used for commit author metadata (repo `.git/config`, global git config, environment variables, agent-level defaults)?

## Reproduction (high level)
1. Configure local/global git email to `agent@thomas.md`.
2. Use the agent workflow to create a commit.
3. Observe commit ownership/author metadata includes Claude identity instead of only the configured email.

title: Support explicit Claude settings in profiles/backend and define mission apply order
body:
## Problem

When running missions with the Claude Code backend, mission bootstrap writes a fresh workspace `.claude/settings.json` and runs with per-mission `HOME` + `CLAUDE_CONFIG(_DIR)`. This can bypass/override user Claude host settings (including commit attribution behavior such as `includeCoAuthoredBy`).

Today, library config profiles expose Claude settings via a typed `ClaudeCodeConfig`, but only a narrow subset is represented and applied.

## Why this matters

Users expect Claude behavior (especially attribution/co-author defaults) to be controlled from profile settings in sandboxed.sh, not by implicit mission-generated defaults.

## Current implementation references

- Per-mission Claude config env and isolated home:
  - `src/api/mission_runner.rs` (sets `HOME`, `XDG_*`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG`)
- Mission workspace writes fresh Claude settings:
  - `src/workspace.rs` `write_claudecode_config(...)` writes `.claude/settings.json` / `settings.local.json`
- Profile Claude config is strongly typed and limited fields are persisted:
  - `src/library/types.rs` (`ClaudeCodeConfig`)
  - `src/library/mod.rs` (`get/save_claudecode_config_for_profile`)
- Dashboard sanitizes Claude settings to a narrow schema for default profile save/sync:
  - `dashboard/src/app/config/settings/page.tsx` (`coerceClaudeCodeConfig`)

## Requested change

Add **explicit Claude settings support** in backend config/profile and define clear apply semantics.

### Minimum scope

1. Add explicit support for Claude attribution/co-author control at profile/backend level
- Include `includeCoAuthoredBy` (or equivalent canonical internal field mapped to Claude settings).
- Keep backward compatibility with existing `ClaudeCodeConfig.attribution`.

2. Define and implement **merge/apply order** for mission startup
- Proposed precedence (highest -> lowest):
  1. Mission request explicit overrides
  2. Workspace-selected config profile (`configs/<profile>/.claudecode/settings.json`)
  3. Library default profile
  4. Generated runtime defaults (MCP/permissions/runtime-only fields)
- Runtime-generated fields should be merged in a way that does not discard user-configured Claude keys.

3. Preserve Claude-native keys in dashboard/profile editing
- Avoid narrowing Claude settings to only `default_model/default_agent/hidden_agents` when saving profile/default settings.

4. Document behavior
- Add docs for:
  - which Claude settings are supported explicitly,
  - where they should be configured,
  - when they are applied,
  - and exact precedence.

## Acceptance criteria

- Setting co-author attribution behavior in a config profile affects new Claude missions consistently.
- User-provided Claude keys are not silently dropped during save/sync.
- Mission bootstrap keeps required runtime fields (MCP/permissions/hooks) while preserving profile/user Claude settings.
- Behavior is documented in docs-site and/or settings UI help text.

title: Move mission auto-title generation to backend for web+iOS parity
body:
## Problem
Mission auto-titling is currently implemented in the web client with browser-local LLM config (`localStorage`). That creates cross-client inconsistency:
- iOS cannot use the same title-generation path/config
- behavior depends on which client created/observed the mission first
- API keys are stored per browser/device rather than centrally

## Goal
Move mission title generation to the backend so web and iOS share one consistent mechanism.

## Proposed architecture
- Add server-side LLM settings (provider/base URL/model/key/enable flag) to backend config.
- Trigger title generation in backend mission pipeline (on first successful assistant message for untitled missions).
- Persist generated title in mission store and emit `mission_title_changed` event as today.
- Keep client-side auto-title disabled/removed once backend path is enabled.

## API + config considerations
- New settings endpoint fields for backend-managed title generation (or reuse existing settings endpoint):
  - `llm_title_enabled`
  - `llm_provider`
  - `llm_base_url`
  - `llm_model`
  - `llm_api_key` (write-only in API responses, masked on read)
- Consider secure storage/encryption at rest for API key if not already available.
- Add explicit health/status check for title-generation provider config validity.

## Client behavior after migration
- Web and iOS should both only display mission titles from backend events/state.
- No client should directly call provider APIs for title generation.
- iOS parity becomes automatic because titles originate from backend.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New missions created from web or iOS get the same backend-generated title behavior.
- [ ] Title generation runs once per mission (best-effort) and never blocks mission execution.
- [ ] Errors are logged server-side without breaking mission flow.
- [ ] API key is not exposed in read APIs/logs.
- [ ] Existing missions/titles remain unchanged.
- [ ] Web client localStorage LLM config path is removed or gated behind a dev flag.

## Migration notes
- Backward compatibility: if backend LLM is not configured, no auto-title generation occurs.
- Optional one-time UI migration message to explain that title generation moved from browser config to server config.

title: LLM roadmap: mission metadata + Cmd+K semantic discovery
body:
## Summary
Use the existing mission LLM capability to improve discovery, navigation, and context quality across clients, with `Cmd+K` as the primary surface.

This issue proposes a phased roadmap with backend-first architecture so behavior is consistent for web and iOS.

## Why
Current LLM usage is mostly title generation. We can get much more value by improving:
- mission metadata quality (title + short description)
- duplicate avoidance
- search relevance in `Cmd+K`
- fast navigation in long mission histories

## Recommended roadmap

### Phase 1 — Metadata foundation (backend-first)
1. Backend-managed `title` + `short_description`
- Generate both when a mission first gets a successful assistant response.
- Persist in mission store and emit events for client updates.

2. Metadata lifecycle updates
- Re-evaluate metadata every 10 messages (or milestone events), only if drift is significant.
- Keep updates best-effort and non-blocking.

3. Anti-duplicate title generation
- Include recent mission titles as negative context in prompt.
- Apply server-side near-duplicate guard and append disambiguator if needed.

### Phase 2 — `Cmd+K` relevance improvements
4. Hybrid search pipeline
- Keep lexical search for recall.
- Re-rank top-N results with LLM for semantic relevance.
- Cache rerank responses by query hash + mission update timestamp.

5. Query expansion
- Expand short/ambiguous queries into likely synonyms/domains before retrieval.

6. Richer result cards
- Show `title` + `short_description` + status + backend in `Cmd+K`.

### Phase 3 — Navigation and action intelligence
7. Jump-to-moment retrieval
- Query examples: “where did we fix session id?”, “show timeout root cause”.
- Return mission + message/event anchor + short rationale.

8. Contextual quick actions in `Cmd+K`
- Suggest actions like Resume, Open failing tool call, Follow-up mission, etc.

## Data model additions
- `missions.short_description` (nullable text)
- `missions.metadata_updated_at`
- optional provenance fields (model/version/source) for generated metadata

## API considerations
- Include `short_description` in mission list/detail payloads.
- Add optional endpoint for semantic search/rerank in `Cmd+K` flow.
- Ensure generated metadata updates are evented for live UI sync.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New missions receive backend-generated title + short description.
- [ ] Metadata refresh after ~10 messages works without blocking mission execution.
- [ ] Duplicate/near-duplicate titles are measurably reduced.
- [ ] `Cmd+K` top results improve for natural-language queries.
- [ ] Web and iOS show identical mission metadata behavior.

## Non-goals (initially)
- Full vector database rollout for all content.
- Generating long descriptions or full narrative reports by default.

## Notes
This roadmap intentionally favors incremental value:
- Phase 1 improves metadata quality immediately.
- Phase 2 improves search UX without major infra changes.
- Phase 3 adds high-value navigation and action intelligence once metadata/retrieval are reliable.

title: Queue UI shows stale queued state after tab/app regains focus
body:
## Summary

When a user unfocuses the browser tab (web) or backgrounds the app (iOS), queued messages that were processed while the window was inactive still appear as "Queued" in the UI when the user returns. The correct state (processed / in chat) only appears after the async reconciliation completes, causing a brief but confusing stale state.

## Reproduction

1. Start a mission and wait for the agent to begin working
2. Send a second message while the agent is busy — it appears in the queue strip with the "Queued" badge
3. Switch to another tab/app and wait for the agent to finish the first message and process the queued one
4. Switch back to the sandboxed.sh tab — the message still shows as queued for a moment before the reload catches up

## Root cause analysis

The dashboard has four sync mechanisms for queue state:

| Mechanism | Trigger | What it does |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| SSE `user_message` | Real-time event with `queued: false` | Updates item's queued flag inline (`control-client.tsx:5007-5025`) |
| SSE `status` | `queue_len` decreases | Calls `syncQueueForMission()` → fetches fresh queue from `/api/control/queue` (`control-client.tsx:4967-4969`) |
| Visibility change | `document.visibilityState === "visible"` | Calls `reloadMissionHistory()` → full parallel fetch of mission + events + queue (`control-client.tsx:6258-6266`) |
| Periodic poll | Every 15 seconds (running missions only) | Same `reloadMissionHistory()` (`control-client.tsx:6269-6277`) |

The problem manifests because:

### Web (Next.js dashboard)

1. **Browser throttling of background tabs.** Chrome and other browsers aggressively throttle background tabs: timers are reduced to 1/sec, `requestAnimationFrame` stops, and while SSE connections stay open, React state updates from event handlers may be batched/deferred. The `user_message { queued: false }` SSE event arrives but React may not commit the state update to the DOM until the tab regains focus.

2. **Stale-then-fresh flash.** When the user refocuses, the visibility change handler fires `reloadMissionHistory()` which is async. Between the moment the tab becomes visible (showing the stale queued state from the last committed render) and when the API response arrives and `setItems()` runs, the user sees the outdated "Queued" badge. This window can be 200-500ms depending on API latency.

3. **`syncQueueForMission` guard.** The `syncingQueueRef` mutex (`control-client.tsx:6164`) prevents concurrent queue syncs. If a status event fires at roughly the same time as the visibility change reload, one of them is skipped, potentially extending the stale window.

### iOS

1. **URLSession stream suspension.** When the app enters the background, iOS suspends the URLSession, which stops SSE delivery entirely. Events emitted during this time are lost — the TCP connection may even be torn down.

2. **Foreground recovery relies solely on `scenePhase`.** The `.onChange(of: scenePhase)` handler (`ControlView.swift:315-326`) calls `reloadMissionFromServer()` when the app becomes active, but this has the same stale-then-fresh flash as the web since it's async. Additionally, if the SSE connection was torn down, the reconnection and the foreground reload race against each other.

## Proposed fixes (ordered by impact)

### 1. Optimistic queue state invalidation on focus (quick win)

When the tab/app regains focus, **immediately clear the `queued` flag on all items** before the async reload confirms. Since the user was away and the agent was working, the overwhelmingly common case is that queued items have been processed.

```tsx
// In visibility change handler (control-client.tsx:6259)
const handleVisibilityChange = () => {
  if (document.visibilityState === "visible" && viewingMissionId) {
    // Immediately mark all items as not-queued to avoid stale flash
    setItems((prev) =>
      prev.map((item) =>
        item.kind === "user" && item.queued ? { ...item, queued: false } : item
      )
    );
    reloadMissionHistory(viewingMissionId);
  }
};
```

The subsequent `reloadMissionHistory` will re-apply correct queued flags if any items are still genuinely queued. The brief false-negative (showing a queued item as not-queued for 200ms) is far less confusing than the current false-positive.

### 2. SSE reconnect with event replay / sequence tracking (robust fix)

Add a monotonic sequence number to SSE events. On reconnection or focus-recovery, the client sends `Last-Event-ID` and the backend replays missed events. This is the standard SSE spec mechanism (`EventSource` supports it natively, but the current `fetch`-based streaming in `api.ts:475-630` doesn't use it).

**Backend changes:**
- Add an incrementing `id:` field to each SSE event in the stream response
- Keep a bounded ring buffer of recent events per mission (last ~100)
- On reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`, replay missed events before resuming live stream

**Frontend changes:**
- Track the last received event ID
- On reconnect, send it as `Last-Event-ID` header
- Process replayed events through the existing handler

### 3. Periodic queue heartbeat while running (incremental)

Reduce the 15-second periodic sync interval to 5 seconds while the agent is actively running and the queue is non-empty. This narrows the window for stale state even without tab focus changes.

```tsx
const syncInterval = queueLen > 0 ? 5_000 : 15_000;
```

### 4. iOS-specific: Background task for SSE keepalive

Use `BGAppRefreshTask` or `URLSessionConfiguration.background` to maintain the SSE connection while the app is in the background. This allows iOS to deliver events even when the app is suspended, eliminating the gap entirely.

## Affected files

- `dashboard/src/app/control/control-client.tsx` — visibility handler, queue sync, SSE processing
- `dashboard/src/lib/api.ts` — SSE streaming, reconnection logic
- `ios_dashboard/SandboxedDashboard/Views/Control/ControlView.swift` — scenePhase handler, stream management
- `ios_dashboard/SandboxedDashboard/Services/APIService.swift` — SSE connection lifecycle
- `src/api/control.rs` — SSE event emission (if implementing sequence tracking)

## Recommendation

**Fix #1** (optimistic invalidation) is the lowest-effort change that eliminates the user-visible symptom. **Fix #2** (SSE sequence tracking) is the principled long-term solution that also fixes other missed-event scenarios (network blips, mobile network switches, etc.). They can be done incrementally — #1 first for immediate relief, #2 as follow-up infrastructure.

title: OpenCode missions timeout: stale processes + plugin install delay
body:
## Problem

OpenCode missions fail with `Timeout waiting for server to start after 5000ms` when starting in container workspaces.

**Mission ID:** `98cd8afc-1e2b-418e-9250-38a2224963e5` (maintain-repo workspace)

## Root Cause

Two compounding issues:

### 1. Stale processes from completed missions

When an OpenCode mission completes, its child processes (`opencode serve`, `oh-my-opencode`) are **never killed** inside the container. They accumulate indefinitely:

- The `maintain-repo` container had zombie processes from mission `b7f1bc53` (completed Feb 22) still running 3 days later
- Multiple `opencode serve` instances on ports 45267, 39285, and 4096
- The container's PID 1 is the old mission's shell process, which `nsenter` uses as the leader

`cleanup_opencode_listeners()` only kills processes on the **newly allocated port**, not stale servers on other ports.

### 2. Plugin installation during `opencode serve` startup

The `.opencode/opencode.json` config includes:
```json
"plugin": ["opencode-openai-codex-auth@latest"]
```

When `opencode serve` starts, it installs this plugin from npm (`@latest` forces a registry check). This installation eats into the **hardcoded 5000ms timeout** in oh-my-opencode's `createOpencodeServer()` (`@opencode-ai/sdk`). If the registry is slow, the server doesn't output `"opencode server listening"` in time and oh-my-opencode gives up.

Previous failed missions confirm npm install is a recurring issue:
```
OpenCode CLI exited with status: exit status: 1. Last stderr: npm install oh-my-opencode-linux-x64
```
(8 occurrences on Feb 22 alone)

## Additional Context

- `sandboxed-sh-prod` systemd service has been dead since Feb 23 (crashed with `Address already in use`). An orphaned process (PID 1977172) is serving port 3000 without systemd supervision or journald logging.
- The container shares the host network namespace, so port conflicts between containers and the host are possible.
- Manual reproduction at ~10:12 UTC succeeded because the plugin was already cached from the failed 09:01 attempt.

## Proposed Fix

### 1. Kill stale opencode processes before starting a new mission

Expand `cleanup_opencode_listeners()` (or add a new cleanup step) to kill **all** `opencode serve` processes inside the container/workspace before launching a new mission, not just those on the allocated port.

### 2. Pre-install opencode plugins before launching oh-my-opencode

Before running `oh-my-opencode run`, run `bun install` (or `opencode serve` briefly) in the `.opencode` config directory so plugins are cached and don't eat into the 5000ms startup timeout.

## Files

- `src/api/mission_runner.rs` — `cleanup_opencode_listeners()` (line ~7099), `run_opencode_turn()` (line ~7428)
- `src/workspace_exec.rs` — `build_nsenter_command()`, container process execution
evidence: OpenCode missions timeout: stale processes + plugin install delay

title: Mission UX: make long-task supervision more repo-centric (branch/diff/files/raw terminal/multi-agent)
body:
## Summary

`sandboxed.sh` has the stronger backend/orchestration model, but the mission UI is still optimized around a mission-event console rather than a repo-centric long-task workspace. After comparing it in depth with `generalaction/emdash`, the biggest UX gap is not visual polish; it is that the user cannot stay inside one surface that combines:

- live agent run
- repo/file tree
- diff/changed files
- branch/base-branch context
- multi-agent comparison
- raw terminal / low-level output when needed

Today the mission creation flow is backend-aware and workspace-aware, but not repo-state-aware, and the control page is excellent for supervision/debugging while still weak for "watch the agent edit code for an hour and inspect what changed without leaving the mission."

## Evidence in current code

- Mission creation is centered on workspace/backend/model selection in [dashboard/src/components/new-mission-dialog.tsx](dashboard/src/components/new-mission-dialog.tsx).
- Mission control exposes strong ops features such as thinking, diagnostics, desktop, queueing, resume/retry, and status panels in [dashboard/src/app/control/control-client.tsx](dashboard/src/app/control/control-client.tsx).
- `/files` currently redirects to `/console`, so repo browsing is not integrated into the mission surface in a first-class way in [dashboard/src/app/files/page.tsx](dashboard/src/app/files/page.tsx).

## Problem

For long coding tasks, the operator loop is currently:

1. Start mission from workspace/backend selections.
2. Watch normalized events.
3. Leave the mission surface to inspect code/diff context elsewhere.
4. Return to mission control to continue supervising.

That is operationally strong, but it is a worse editing/supervision loop than `emdash`, where task terminal, file tree, diff, branch state, and multi-agent tabs are part of one workspace.

## Proposed direction

Bring the best parts of `emdash` into the mission UX without losing the orchestration strengths that make `sandboxed.sh` better infrastructure.

### 1. Make mission creation repo-aware

Extend the new mission dialog to show:

- current branch
- optional base branch / target branch
- changed files count / dirty state
- recent commit or PR/issue context if present
- a clear "open as coding workspace" mode for long tasks

This would let users launch long tasks with actual repo context instead of only runtime context.

### 2. Add a repo workspace pane to mission control

The control screen should support an IDE-like split layout:

- center: mission stream / normalized events
- left: file tree + changed files
- right or bottom: diff / patch / raw terminal / diagnostics

The goal is that a user can watch the agent, inspect edited files, inspect diffs, and jump back to tool output without switching products/pages.

### 3. Expose raw backend console alongside normalized events

The normalized event view is useful, but long-task supervision also benefits from a raw PTY/CLI transcript toggle:

- raw terminal view for debugging odd CLI behavior
- normalized event view for tool understanding
- easy switching between them in the same mission

This is especially important when diagnosing model/tool hangs or partial outputs.

### 4. Add first-class multi-agent comparison for the same task

`emdash` is notably better at showing parallel agent/worktree attempts. `sandboxed.sh` should support:

- launching N variants of the same mission prompt
- per-variant branch/worktree isolation
- tabs or columns for each run
- shared diff comparison across variants

This would materially improve the "long task with several agents" workflow.

### 5. Reduce cognitive load for the default coding path

Mission control currently exposes many strong operator features at once. For the common case of "run one coding agent on one long task," the default UI should be simpler:

- compact default layout
- advanced ops panels behind secondary toggles
- repo + diff visibility promoted ahead of lower-frequency diagnostics

## Suggested implementation areas

- `dashboard/src/components/new-mission-dialog.tsx`
- `dashboard/src/app/control/control-client.tsx`
- `dashboard/src/app/files/page.tsx`

This likely also needs a lightweight backend API for repo state metadata per workspace/mission:

- current branch
- dirty state
- changed files
- base branch hints
- maybe active PR metadata when available

## Acceptance criteria

- A user can start a mission with visible branch/repo context.
- A user can inspect file tree and changed files without leaving mission control.
- A user can inspect diffs for edited files in the same mission surface.
- A user can switch between normalized mission events and raw terminal output.
- A user can compare multiple agent runs for one task in a single mission workspace.
- The default long-task path is less cluttered than today while advanced ops controls remain available.

## Why this matters

`sandboxed.sh` already wins on same-server sandboxing, queueing, lifecycle control, stall detection, and remote execution. The main product gap versus `emdash` is the operator workspace for long coding tasks. Closing that gap would improve day-to-day usability without requiring the project to give up its stronger backend model.
