title: build(rc-player): turn on explicitApi and an API-dump gate for the player modules
body:
Independent of #4056 / #4058 / #4059 / #4060 — no shared files, can start immediately and land in any order.

## Why

The player modules are written as though `explicitApi` were on — `public` modifiers throughout `rc-player/compose`, `runtime`, `protocol`, `trace` — but it is set nowhere. There is no `explicitApi` in `build-logic/`, in the root build, or in `gradle.properties`. The discipline is convention, and a `public` that should have been `internal` compiles silently.

This matters more than usual right now: #4056, #4058, #4059 and #4060 are all reshaping the public surface at once, and nothing mechanically reports what that surface became.

## What

1. Enable `explicitApi()` for the four library modules — `:rc-player-protocol`, `:rc-player-runtime`, `:rc-player-compose`, `:rc-player-trace`. Not `:rc-player-wasm` (an executable), `:rc-player-profile` (an application, per its own build comment), `:rc-player-metrics` or `:rc-player-compat-tests` (fixture generators).
2. Add an API-dump gate so surface changes show up in review as a diff. `docs/API_STABILITY.md` notes Kotlin BCV is not wired anywhere in the repo; this would be the first module set to have it. Whether that argues for doing it here first or for solving it repo-wide is a real question — say which on the issue.

Expect step 1 to surface genuine over-exposure. Two candidates already visible:

- `rcResolveSystemTheme` (`RcSystemTheme.kt:27`) is `public` but has no caller outside the module — #4058 has to decide whether it stays public anyway.
- `RcPlayerState`'s full surface, including `setNamedValue` (`RcPlayerState.kt:1057`) and the `applyScope`/`applyColorTheme` family, is public. Some of that is the player's own plumbing rather than a host contract.

Neither is a reason to hold this issue — record what turns up and let the API workstreams decide, rather than making those calls here.

## Not in scope

Actually publishing these modules to Maven Central. No `rc-player/*` module applies `composeai.maven-publishing` today, and that is a separate decision — `docs/design/RC_CMP_WASM_PLAYER.md` still has the player at "implementation in progress" and gated on parity with the AndroidX Java player. This issue makes the surface *legible*, which is a prerequisite either way and is worth having whether or not publishing follows.

## Test plan

- `./gradlew :rc-player-protocol:allTests :rc-player-runtime:allTests :rc-player-compose:allTests :rc-player-trace:allTests` — `explicitApi` is a compile-time gate, so a clean build across all targets is the check.
- iOS and Wasm compile tasks specifically, since `expect`/`actual` declarations (`RcTracePlatform` is an `expect object`) have their own explicit-visibility rules that the desktop build will not exercise.
- If BCV lands: commit the initial dumps in the same PR and confirm CI fails on an unrecorded surface change.

Not `:rc-player-wasm` (an executable), `:rc-player-profile` (an application, per its own build comment), `:rc-player-metrics` or `:rc-player-compat-tests` (fixture generators).

title: publish: `:rc-player-trace` to Maven Central
body:
Part of publishing the Remote Compose player stack. **Gated behind the API work** — #4056 (surface), #4058, #4059, #4060, and #4062 (explicitApi + API dump). Publishing before those land ships a surface we are actively rewriting.

Bottom of the dependency chain (`trace ← protocol ← runtime ← compose`), so this is the first to land.

## What

Apply `composeai.maven-publishing` and declare coordinates:

```kotlin
composeAiMavenPublishing {
  coordinates(
    artifactId = "rc-player-trace",
    displayName = "Remote Compose Player — Tracing",
    description = "Multiplatform tracing facade for the CMP Remote Compose player …",
  )
}
```

## Known blockers specific to this module

**1. `jvm("desktop")` must become unnamed `jvm()`.** `runtimes/slots/build.gradle.kts:35` records the decision, in a published KMP module, with reasoning: the published JVM artifact should carry the conventional `-jvm` classifier matching `:preview-annotations`, and `-desktop` misnames bytecode that Android also resolves. All four player modules currently use `jvm("desktop")`. Renaming the target changes every `desktopMain`/`desktopTest` source-set name and the `:rc-player-*:desktopTest` task paths that `ci.yml` and the profiling docs reference.

**2. No published module has iOS targets yet.** This would be the first (`iosX64`, `iosArm64`, `iosSimulatorArm64`). Expect the klib/signing path to need work that the existing jvm+wasmJs precedent does not cover.

**3. `androidx.tracing` is deliberately `implementation`, not `api`.** The module doc explains why — keeping androidx types off the compile classpath is what stops a call site being written so it only compiles on desktop. Confirm the POM records it as `runtime` scope and that a consumer tracing through `rcTrace`/`RcTrace` needs nothing else.

## Not in scope

The release-chain wiring — this module joins the existing `release.yml` / `snapshot.yml` flow like any other. If it turns out the player modules need their own cadence, that is a separate discussion.

title: publish: `:rc-player-protocol` to Maven Central
body:
Part of publishing the Remote Compose player stack. **Gated behind the API work** — #4056, #4058, #4059, #4060, #4062. Depends on #4063 (`:rc-player-trace`) being published first.

Artifact: `ee.schimke.composeai:rc-player-protocol`. This is the `.rc` wire codec and operation model — plausibly the most independently useful artifact in the stack, since it is consumable without taking any Compose dependency at all.

## Known blockers specific to this module

**1. Generated sources must reach the sources jar.** `GenerateRcOperationManifest` (`rc-player/protocol/build.gradle.kts:6`) generates the opcode table from `rc-operations.manifest`. The vanniktech `SourcesJar.Sources()` path needs the generated directory wired in, or consumers get a sources jar with a hole where `RcOperationInventory` should be.

**2. `jvm("desktop")` → unnamed `jvm()`** — see #4063 for why; the same rename applies here.

**3. iOS klib publishing** — first time in this repo, same as #4063.

## Worth deciding here rather than later

`RcTheme` (`RcModel.kt:352`) is a published wire type carrying `SYSTEM`/`UNSPECIFIED`/`DARK`/`LIGHT` constants, and #4058 introduces a separate host-facing `RcPlayerTheme` enum in the compose module. Two similarly-named public types across two published artifacts is a documentation problem the moment both are consumable. Make sure the KDoc on each says plainly which one a consumer wants — the protocol one is what the decoder produces, not what a host passes.

Same question for `RcOperationProfiles` (`CMP_WASM_ALPHA16`, `CMP_IOS_ALPHA16`): those names encode an alpha level, and publishing makes them a compatibility surface. Decide whether they are public API or should be internal before the first release rather than after.

title: publish: `:rc-player-compose` to Maven Central
body:
Part of publishing the Remote Compose player stack. **Gated behind the API work** — #4056, #4058, #4059, #4060, #4062. Depends on #4065 (`:rc-player-runtime`).

Artifact: `ee.schimke.composeai:rc-player-compose`. The one most consumers actually want — it carries `RcComposePlayer`, and it is the module whose entire public surface #4056 is rewriting. Land it last.

## Known blockers specific to this module

**1. Its target set does not match its siblings, and that is visible to consumers.** Per the module's own build comment, there is no `iosX64()` here: CMP 1.11 dropped the Intel-iOS-simulator variant, while `trace`/`protocol`/`runtime` still publish it. So a consumer on `iosX64` resolves three of the four artifacts and fails on the fourth. Decide before release whether to drop `iosX64` from the whole stack for consistency or document the asymmetry — silently publishing a stack that only partly resolves on one target is the worst of the three options.

**2. Compose Multiplatform version in the POM.** This is the only module in the stack depending on CMP, and the compose-compiler/runtime pairing is a hard constraint for consumers. Check what the published POM records and whether it belongs in the compatibility matrix at `docs/RENDERER_COMPATIBILITY.md` alongside the existing AGP × Kotlin × Compose rows.

**3. `jvm("desktop")` → unnamed `jvm()`** — see #4063. Higher impact here: `desktopTest` is the whole render-test suite.

## Sequencing

Every parameter of this module's entry point is being retyped by #4058, #4059 and #4060, and #4061 may still change the `RcTypefaceLoader.Default` contract afterwards. Publishing before #4061 settles means either shipping a `Default` that resolves nothing and changing it later, or holding the first release for it. Prefer holding — a default that starts resolving fonts it previously didn't is a behaviour change consumers cannot see coming from a version bump.

title: publish: distribute the Wasm player as a consumable bundle
body:
Part of publishing the Remote Compose player stack. **Gated behind the API work** — #4056 and the parameter workstreams. Independent of the Maven issues (#4063–#4066); this is a different distribution problem, not a Maven artifact.

## Today

`:rc-player-wasm` is `binaries.executable()` with `outputModuleName = "rcPlayer"`, assembled by a `wasmPlayerDist` `Sync` task (`rc-player/wasm/build.gradle.kts:31`) into a folder containing the compiled module, `skiko.mjs`, `skiko.wasm` and `index.html`.

The only way to consume it is to build this repo and point `compose-preview serve --wasm-dir` at the output. There is no published bundle. Anyone wanting a Remote Compose player in a web page has to clone and run Gradle.

## What to decide

1. **npm package, or a versioned bundle attached to GitHub Releases, or both?** The CLI already vendors a built JS player at `cli/src/main/resources/rc-player/bundle.js` precisely to keep Node out of the pure-JVM Gradle build (`docs/design/RC_CMP_WASM_PLAYER.md`) — whatever is chosen should not reintroduce that coupling.
2. **What is the embed contract?** `Main.kt` already defines one: `?src=`, `?theme=`, `?fontsBase=`, `?rcTrace=`, `?allowExternalImagePlaceholders=`, plus `window.rcPlayerLoad(src)` for document swap and a readiness marker for hosts to wait on. That is a real public API and is currently documented only in the source. Publishing means writing it down and versioning it.
3. **Size budget.** `wasmPlayerDist` already size-checks. Whether that budget becomes a published guarantee is worth deciding rather than inheriting.

## Sequencing note

`docs/design/RC_CMP_WASM_PLAYER.md` says the vendored TypeScript player stays until the CMP/Wasm lane passes the replacement gates, and that it "supports more operations today". Publishing the Wasm bundle as a consumable while it is still the *less* capable of the two players needs a clear statement of which one an external user should reach for — otherwise the answer depends on which document they found first.

title: publish: ship the iOS player as an XCFramework consumable from Swift
body:
Part of publishing the Remote Compose player stack. **Gated behind the API work** — #4056 and the parameter workstreams. Independent of the Maven issues (#4063–#4066).

## Today

`:rc-player-compose` builds a static framework per iOS target (`baseName = "RcComposePlayer"`), and `RcComposeViewController.kt` is a purpose-built UIKit entry point returning a `UIViewController`. So the iOS story is *designed* — it just has no delivery mechanism. The repo contains no XCFramework assembly task, no `Package.swift`, and no podspec.

A Swift consumer today would have to add this Gradle build to their project and depend on the KMP module directly.

## What

1. An XCFramework task bundling `iosArm64` + `iosSimulatorArm64`. Note `iosX64` does not exist for this module — CMP 1.11 dropped the Intel simulator variant (see the module's build comment and #4066), so the XCFramework covers device and Apple-silicon simulator only. Intel Macs are out, and that should be stated rather than discovered.
2. SPM and/or CocoaPods distribution — decide which. SPM needs a `Package.swift` referencing a binary target plus somewhere to host the zip with a checksum; GitHub Releases is the obvious candidate given the existing release chain.
3. CI coverage. `ci.yml` currently compiles the iOS *test* targets (`:rc-player-compose:compileTestKotlinIosArm64` and friends) but never links or packages a framework, so framework assembly would be newly exercised — and the CI comment at `ci.yml:377` notes `linkDebugTestIosSimulatorArm64` has died before. Expect this step to need real work.

## Surface question

`RcComposeViewController` takes `theme: Int` and `fontFamilies: Map<String, RcFontFaces>` today; #4058 and #4060 change both. A Kotlin enum and a Kotlin interface each cross the Swift boundary differently from an `Int` and a `Map` — worth checking how `RcPlayerTheme` and `RcTypefaceLoader` actually read from Swift *before* those land, since it may be the one place where the nicer Kotlin API is the worse Swift one. If so, say so on #4058/#4060 while they are still open.

Also: `forwardIosPlayerEvent` exists as an `internal` seam, and `RcPlayerEvent` is a sealed interface — sealed hierarchies flatten unhelpfully in Objective-C interop. Check what a Swift consumer actually sees in an `onEvent` callback.

title: `@OverrideVariant.kitAxis` / `kitValue` are dead metadata — nothing downstream reads them
body:
Follow-up to #4073, and a correction to its "Also worth having" section. That section said `@OverrideVariant` "already has `kitAxis` / `kitValue` for exactly this" and proposed adding them to `@CatalogVariant`. **Adding them there would produce a second pair of fields nothing reads**, because the existing pair is already inert.

## The finding

The fields are declared, documented, discovered and serialised:

- `OverrideVariant.kt` declares them, with a worked example (`kitAxis = "Show avatar"`, `kitValue = "True"`).
- `PreviewDiscovery.kt` reads them into `OverrideVariantSpec`.
- Both `PreviewData.kt` mirrors carry them, so they reach `previews.json`.

And then nothing consumes them:

```
$ grep -n "kitAxis\|kitValue" design-map/design-map.mjs design-map/emit-design-map.mjs
(no matches)

$ grep -ro "kitAxis\|kitValue" @design-parity/kit-index@0.1.51
(no matches)
```

`design-map.mjs` never projects them into the sidecar, so they cannot reach a resolver even in principle — and the resolver keys purely on `seeds` regardless. The annotation's own KDoc says they are "metadata only: they do not change the preview override seed," which is accurate; what it does not say is that no reader exists.

## Why it matters

This is the difference between a catalog naming the Compose-side value and having to spell the kit's. m3-catalog#130 folded `DatePicker/Range` onto `DatePicker/Modal` and had to write:

```kotlin
props = ["type=full-screen (range)"]
```

`type=range` resolves to nothing against the kit's `Type=Full-screen (range)` — silently, dropping the node. The natural fix is exactly what `kitAxis` / `kitValue` are described as doing, and it is unavailable: a kit spelling, parentheses and all, is now load-bearing in catalog source, where it will rot the next time the kit renames a variant value.

## What the fix actually needs

Three steps, and the middle one is in another repo — worth knowing before anyone plans this as a one-line annotation change:

1. **`design-map.mjs`** — project a declaration's `kitAxis` / `kitValue` into the sidecar beside its `seeds`, so a resolver can see them at all.
2. **`@design-parity/kit-index`** — prefer an explicit kit axis/value over the seed's own spelling when matching a declaration to a component-set variant. This is the load-bearing half, and it ships as a published package that catalogs pin by version, so it lands on its own release cadence.
3. **`@CatalogVariant`** — gain `kitAxis` / `kitValue` once 1 and 2 mean something, so a folded component can name both sides too.

Sequenced the other way round, each step is inert on its own.

## Related

A prop that resolves to nothing should not fail silently — the `type=range` miss cost a node with no diagnostic anywhere. That warning belongs in the resolver alongside step 2, and it is worth having even if none of the above is done: it turns a silent wrong answer into a loud one.

Also worth deciding as part of step 2: whether a variant can be addressed by *set + variant properties* rather than by seed spelling at all, which is the version of this that survives a kit re-publish renumbering nodes.
comments:
Started on this, in the order the issue lays out — steps 2 and 3 first, since each is inert without the other and step 2 ships on its own release cadence.

- **Step 2** (the load-bearing half): design-parity#356. `VariantSeed` gains `kitAxis` / `kitValue`; a declaration replaces the alias tables for that seed rather than being tried alongside them, is still checked against what the set publishes, and gets its own `explainUnresolved` reason (`kind: "declared"`) reported ahead of the other three — it names the spelling that missed and what the set does publish there. The "related" half of this issue, a prop that resolves to nothing failing loudly, already landed as design-parity#352 and this builds the declaration case on top of it.
- **Steps 1 and 3**: #4094. The projection carries a declaration onto the seed it belongs to, so it reaches the sidecar at all, and `@CatalogVariant` gains the same pair.

Two things worth recording from doing it.

**The dead-metadata finding was right, and the fix is smaller than the issue feared.** No annotation had to change shape; `@OverrideVariant`'s existing pair simply had to be projected. The only new API surface is the same two fields on `@CatalogVariant`.

**One limit is now explicit rather than assumed.** The annotation carries one `kitAxis` / `kitValue` pair per variant, so a cell seeding two knobs gives no way to say which of them the axis names. Rather than pick one — which pins the wrong axis and resolves confidently to the wrong node — the projection reports it (`diagnostics.unplacedDeclarations`, printed by the emitter) and drops the declaration, leaving the seeds to resolve on their own spelling. A per-seed form is the natural extension if a real cell ever wants it; nothing in m3-catalog does today.

Still open here: the last paragraph of this issue — whether a variant can be addressed by *set + variant properties* rather than by seed spelling at all, which is the version that survives a kit re-publish renumbering nodes. Neither PR touches that.

All three steps are done, released, and in use. m3-catalog#143 merged, which is the first real consumer.

| Step | Landed | Released |

The motivating case now reads as it should, and the join survived it: 59 components and 543 kit nodes both unchanged, with `51954:18254` still resolved for the range picker.

```kotlin

                kitAxis = "Type", kitValue = "Full-screen (range)")
```

Two things worth recording for whoever reads this next.

**The "related" ask — a prop that resolves to nothing should fail loudly — is covered**, by design-parity#352's `explainUnresolved` plus the new `declared` reason on top of it. A declaration naming something the set does not publish is reported ahead of the other three reasons, with the spelling that missed and what the set does publish. It is the only miss whose fix is in catalog source, so it outranks them.

**A declaration is authoritative, not a hint**, and that turned out to be the whole design problem. Twenty-one review findings across the two design-parity PRs, and nearly all of them were the same shape: a declaration that could still be *silently* ignored (dropped by a seed merge, unreachable on a folder-modelled family, invisible to the property path) or *silently* honoured wrongly (a punctuation twin, a numeric collision, a fusion that discarded the other seed). One rule got withdrawn for that reason — containment-based fusion for scripts that write no spaces, since `選択` is a substring of `未選択` and the check would have cited the node drawing the opposite state. That gap is documented rather than papered over.

title: `SharedElementFilmstripPreview` is not deterministic — it re-renders differently on unrelated PRs
body:
The filmstrip's whole reason for existing is that it is the *static, diffable* counterpart to the GIF preview. Its KDoc says so:

> a **deterministic filmstrip** … each panel freezes the transition at an exact fraction with `SeekableTransitionState.seekTo`, so … a visual-diff bot can compare it pixel-for-pixel without the frame-timing jitter a GIF carries.

It does carry that jitter. The render changes on PRs that cannot possibly affect it, which makes the diff bot's most valuable signal — "this is the one thing your change moved" — noise on the one preview built to be noise-free.

## Evidence

`renders/samples:android/SharedElementFilmstripPreview_Shared_Element_Filmstrip-a8af1cd8.png` changed in **ten** of the most recent render commits, across five unrelated PRs:

| Render commit | PR | What that PR touched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1a5569c` | #4094 | design-map projection + annotation fields (no renderer, no samples) |
| `32f726b` | #4092 | CI workflow repair |
| `335e63e`, `c70d8d6` | #4090 | `serve` daemon a11y extension |
| `f9115ef` | #4074 | — |
| `3b035b6`, `fd646f3`, `a1f82b1`, `1174a82` | #4069 | — |
| `64af78f` | #4053 | — |

None of those touch `samples/android` or the render path. Note #4069 alone produced four consecutive renders that each differed from the last.

Pixel-diffing #4094's before/after (`4550925` → `1a5569c`):

```
sizes            (893, 2153) both
bbox             (32, 511) – (441, 672)
changed px       57,317 / 1,922,629 = 2.98 %
max channel diff 164
```

One contiguous band, roughly one panel of the five, differing by a lot rather than by a rounding hair — the shape of a panel rendered at a *different point in the transition*, not of a re-encode.

## Likely cause

```kotlin
val seekState = remember { SeekableTransitionState(FilmScreen.Collapsed) }
// One-shot seek to a constant fraction; the panel renders the transition frozen there.
LaunchedEffect(Unit) {
  seekState.seekTo(fraction = fraction, targetState = FilmScreen.Expanded)
}
```

`seekTo` **suspends**. The constant fraction makes the *destination* deterministic; it does not make the capture wait for the panel to arrive there. Whether a given panel has finished seeking when the frame is grabbed is a race between five coroutines and the renderer, so a run can capture a panel still at (or part-way to) its collapsed start — exactly one band differing, the rest identical.

## Options

1. **Make the capture wait for the seek.** The renderer already has an idle/await seam for animated previews; if a preview can declare "not ready until my effects have settled", this becomes deterministic by construction and every future filmstrip-shaped preview gets it too.
2. **Seek without suspending** — drive the five panels from one already-settled state, or set the fraction where composition can read it synchronously, so there is nothing to race.
3. **Failing both, stop claiming determinism**: drop the preview from the diffable set and correct the KDoc, so a reviewer is not taught to read its diffs as meaningful.

The first is the one that pays forward, and it is the same gap that would bite any preview whose content settles in a `LaunchedEffect`.

Raised from #4094, where this showed up as the only "Changed" entry against a text-and-data-only diff.
comments:
Second data point, and it isolates which side moves.

#4094 re-ran the preview diff after merging `main`, and again reports exactly one changed variant — this filmstrip — with a fresh pair of renders (`125c759` → `91c1ec1`). Comparing all four PNGs across the two runs:

| Comparison | Differs? |
| --- | --- |
| run 1 base → head (`4550925` → `1a5569c`) | yes — bbox (32, 511)–(441, 672), 2.98 % |
| run 2 base → head (`125c759` → `91c1ec1`) | yes — bbox (32, 511)–(844, 1704), 7.42 % |
| **head 1 vs head 2** | **no — pixel-identical** |
| **base 1 vs base 2** | **yes — bbox (32, 511)–(844, 1704)** |

So the PR's own render is stable across two independent runs, and it is the **baseline** that moved. The two baselines are renders of `a2cf3e7` and `ba309d9`, and nothing between those commits touches `samples/android` — #4095 changed the Wear catalog. Two renders of unchanged source, differing across roughly three of the five panels.

That also rules out the reading that some source change was quietly moving the image: there is no source change, and the run-to-run variation is larger (7.42 %, spanning multiple panels) than the "difference" the bot attributes to the PR (2.98 %, one panel). The signal is smaller than the noise it sits in.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Third run, and it corrects my last comment: **both sides move.** I said the head render was stable and only the baseline drifted — that was true of two samples and is not true in general.

Adding run 3 (`7e7a68e` → `0e2aa6b`) to the matrix:

| Comparison | Differs? |
| --- | --- |
| head 1 vs head 2 | no — pixel-identical |
| **head 1 vs head 3** | **yes** — bbox (32, 511)–(844, 1704) |
| **head 2 vs head 3** | **yes** — same region |
| base 1 vs base 2 | yes |
| **base 2 vs base 3** | **yes** — bbox (32, 511)–(707, 1218) |
| run 3 base → head | yes — bbox (32, 511)–(707, 1218) |

Three runs of the same PR produced three different renders on each side, each differing in a different region. Two identical heads in a row was luck, not stability — which is worth knowing, because "the head is stable" would have suggested the baseline pipeline as the culprit and sent someone looking in the wrong place.

The reading that survives all three runs is the simple one: **this preview renders differently every time, on whichever side you look at**, and the run-to-run variation is consistently larger than the base→head difference the bot reports as this PR's change.

Given #4096 — where a settle window turned out to under-settle in proportion to how many previews had rendered ahead of the subject — it is worth asking whether this filmstrip has the same shape of bug rather than the `LaunchedEffect` race I originally guessed. Five panels each seeking their own `SeekableTransitionState` would be sensitive to exactly that kind of order-dependent time budget, and it would explain why the differing region moves between runs instead of always being the same panel.

---

title: `VS Code Extension E2E (interactive-*)` times out waiting for renders — a different scenario each run
body:
The interactive E2E shards fail on roughly half the runs, and **never twice in the same place**. Every failure is a timeout waiting for a render to appear on disk, and the scenario that draws the short straw moves around — which makes a red result here carry no information about the diff that triggered it.

## Four consecutive shard runs on one PR (#4094, `d60f5a0` / `c7c5b5b`)

| Shard | Run | A | B | C | D / E–G | Failure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `interactive-e-g` | 1 | — | — | — | E ✗, F ✓, G ✓ | E: panel resolved to empty state — `0 code preview(s)` from empty class outputs |
| `interactive-e-g` | 2 (re-run) | — | — | — | all ✓ | — |
| `interactive-a-d` | 1 | ✓ 115s | ✗ | ✓ 1.7s | ✓ 36s | B: `Timed out after 180000ms` waiting for a capture |
| `interactive-a-d` | 2 (re-run) | ✓ 109s | ✓ 112s | ✗ | ✓ 35s | C: `Timed out after 480000ms` waiting for captures |

Same commit, same shard, two runs: **B fails then passes; C passes in 1.7 s then times out after 8 minutes.** A scenario that completes in 1.7 s on one run and cannot finish in 480 s on the next is not failing on its own logic.

## What each failure actually says

Two distinct symptoms, both upstream of the assertions:

**Renders never arrive.** Scenario C's message names three captures still missing after eight minutes:
```
latest cmp setPreviews: 6 preview(s); captures not on disk:
  AppPreview-02e12488.png, Pixel8SystemUiPreview_Pixel_8_Night-750cb3e0.png, Pixel8SystemUiPreview_Pixel_8-67f4e782.png
```

**Class outputs come back empty**, which the plugin itself diagnoses:
```
composePreview: module 'cmp' has 18 source file(s) declaring @Preview but its active class
outputs contain 0 .class files. A compile task may have restored an empty build-cache entry;
rerun with --no-build-cache --rerun-tasks.
```

## Why this is worth fixing rather than re-running

The scenarios are slow enough to be racing their own budget: A takes ~110 s of a job that runs four scenarios, and the suite spawns real Gradle invocations that it also **cancels mid-flight** by design (`terminating gradlew pid …` appears throughout). A cancelled `composePreviewCompile` is exactly how a half-written class output directory — and the empty-cache-entry path above — comes about. So the harness's own cancellation may be manufacturing the condition its next scenario then trips over.

Three things that would each help, cheapest first:

1. **Make the wait diagnostic.** The timeouts already name which captures are missing; adding whether the render task *ran*, was cancelled, or was served `FROM-CACHE` would tell a reader in one line which of the two symptoms they have.
2. **Bound the cancellation damage.** After cancelling a compile, treat the module's class outputs as dirty — the plugin's own advice (`--no-build-cache --rerun-tasks`) applied automatically rather than left to the next scenario to discover.
3. **Give the render-dependent waits a budget proportional to a cold render.** 180 s is under two of scenario A's own render passes on the same runner.

Related: #4097 is a different preview whose *output* is nondeterministic; this is about renders not arriving at all. They meet at the same place — a CI signal that costs a re-run to interpret.

Raised from #4094, where this shard has now failed twice in two different scenarios against a diff that touches no compile, cache, or render path. Not re-running it a third time.

title: Studio: typing in the composer during a reply removes the Stop generating button
body:
### Summary

While a reply is generating, typing anything into the composer replaces the **Stop generating** button with **Queue message**. There is then no way to stop the running generation until the composer is cleared again.

This is the long-generation case specifically: the longer a reply runs, the more likely a user is to start typing their next message while they wait, and that is exactly the moment they lose the ability to stop it.

### Reproduction

1. Load any model and send a prompt that produces a long reply.
2. While it is still streaming, note the round button at the right of the composer is a square **Stop generating**.
3. Type a single character into the composer.
4. The button becomes an up-arrow **Queue message**. Stop is gone.
5. Select all and delete the composer text. Stop reappears.

### Cause

`studio/frontend/src/components/assistant-ui/thread.tsx`, in the composer's send slot. While the thread is running the button is chosen by a single ternary:

```tsx
<AuiIf condition={({ thread }) => thread.isRunning}>
  {queueDisabled ? (
    ... aria-label="Stop generating" ...
  ) : (
    ... aria-label="Queue message" ...
  )}
</AuiIf>
```

and `queueDisabled` is

```tsx
queueDisabled={
  disableQueue ||
  !(canQueueCurrentPrompt || canQueuePastedTextPrompt)
}
```

So `queueDisabled` is true only while there is nothing queueable. Typing makes the prompt queueable, which flips `queueDisabled` to false, which swaps Stop for Queue. The two actions share one slot, and queueing wins.

### Suggested direction

Stop and Queue are not alternatives from the user's point of view: one ends the current run, the other schedules the next. They probably want to coexist while the thread is running rather than share a slot. Not proposing a specific layout here, since that is a design call.

### Provenance

Found while verifying #9012, #9014 and #9054. Present identically on both the merge base and the head of those PRs, so it pre-dates all three and should not be bisected onto them. Observed on Chromium via Playwright against a local build; the ternary above is on current `main`.

title: Studio: no sampling seed in the UI, so a generation cannot be reproduced
body:
### Summary

There is no way to pin a sampling seed from the Studio UI, so a generation cannot be reproduced. The backend already accepts and forwards a seed, so the gap is only in the frontend's parameter set.

### Detail

`InferenceParams` in `studio/frontend/src/features/chat/types/runtime.ts` is the full set of knobs the UI can send:

```
temperature, topP, topK, minP, repetitionPenalty, presencePenalty,
maxSeqLength, maxTokens, systemPrompt, systemVariables,
checkpoint, trustRemoteCode, fastMode
```

No `seed`. Meanwhile `seed` is a recognised field on the backend side (it appears in `studio/backend/assets/configs/inference_defaults.json`) and is forwarded to llama-server, so the capability exists and is simply unreachable from the UI.

### Why it matters, with a concrete cost

This is not hypothetical. While verifying #9054 I needed to establish whether two Studio builds rendered the same reply, which requires the model to emit the same tokens twice. On this host it does not:

| configuration | run A | run B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| as shipped (`--parallel 4`, spec decoding on, UI sampling) | 488 chars | 373 chars |
| temperature 0, top_k 1, top_p 1, seed forced at the wire | 3,960 chars | 150 chars |
| `n_parallel=1`, speculative decoding off, temperature 0, top_k 1, seed forced | identical, repeatedly |

Getting a reproducible generation at all required rewriting the outgoing `/v1/chat/completions` body from outside the app with a Playwright route handler, because the UI cannot express a seed. Anyone comparing two builds, chasing a regression, or filing a reproducible bug report hits the same wall.

Note the seed alone is not sufficient (row two shows that), but it is necessary, and it is the only one of the three levers that has no UI at all.

### Suggested direction

Add `seed` to `InferenceParams` and surface it in the Run settings panel, blank meaning "unset" so nothing changes for users who do not touch it.

### Provenance

Found while verifying #9012, #9014 and #9054. Independent of all three: it is a missing field, present identically on their merge bases and heads, so it should not be bisected onto them.

title: [Studio Bug] Cached Qwen3.5-9B is re-downloaded, stalls on Xet, then fails after 14 minutes
body:
## Environment

**Where are you using Unsloth?**

- [x] Studio desktop application
- [ ] Studio web UI (`unsloth studio`)
- [ ] Unsloth CLI
- [ ] Python package or notebook
- [ ] Colab or Kaggle

**Operating system and version:**

- Windows 11 Pro, version 10.0.26200 (build 26200)
- Python 3.13.13

**GPU model(s) and accelerator backend:**

- AMD Radeon PRO W7800 48GB
- AMD driver 32.0.23033.1002
- ROCm / HIP 7.13.99004
- One GPU visible

**Versions:**

- Unsloth Studio Desktop: 0.1.800-beta
- Unsloth: 2026.8.18
- Unsloth Zoo: 2026.8.12
- PyTorch: 2.11.0+rocm7.13.0
- Transformers: 5.3.0
- Triton: 3.7.1
- huggingface_hub: 1.27.0
- hf_xet: 1.6.0
- httpx: 0.28.1

## What happened?

A cached `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` model repeatedly took a very long time to start and failed. Studio displayed:

> Starting model... Switching models. Loading cached model into memory.

However, the backend was actually downloading model data from Hugging Face.

After several failed attempts, the same local LoRA adapter eventually loaded successfully in 61.2 seconds. This success happened **before** I manually completed the five missing cache files described below, so I cannot claim that cache completion caused the success. The behavior appears intermittent.

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Install and launch Unsloth Studio Desktop on Windows with the AMD ROCm build.
2. Have `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` present in the Hugging Face cache and a local LoRA adapter whose base model is `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`.
3. Select the cached base model or the local LoRA in Studio.
4. Observe that the UI says it is loading a cached model into memory, while backend logs show Xet or HTTPS downloading.
5. Wait for the load to stall or fail.

**Expected behavior:**

- A complete cached weight shard should be reused without downloading it again.
- Missing small metadata/tokenizer files should be fetched independently.
- Interrupted downloads should be resumable or retried automatically.
- The UI should distinguish “loading from cache” from “downloading from Hugging Face” and show real progress.

**Actual behavior:**

The first observed attempt spent approximately 14 minutes 27 seconds in the load request and then failed during an HTTP download:

```text
Error loading model: peer closed connection without sending complete message body
(received 913201896 bytes, expected 5335092639)

Model load failed with 500 after the response committed
POST /api/inference/load ... process_time_ms=867293.75
```

Another attempt ended with the inference worker disappearing:

```text
RuntimeError: The inference worker stopped unexpectedly while loading the model.
Details: process missing.

POST /api/inference/load ... process_time_ms=143504.62
```

A later attempt showed Xet stalling, followed by the HTTPS fallback:

```text
Subprocess status: Downloading (xet transport)...
Subprocess reported stall: Download appears stalled (xet transport) -- no progress for 30s
Download stalled for 'Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B' -- retrying with HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1
Inference subprocess did not exit gracefully, terminating
Spawning fresh inference subprocess for 'Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B'
(transformers 5.x, attempt 2/2, xet disabled)
```

The fallback then reported:

```text
Unsafe partial for 'Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B' could not be cleared;
forcing a clean HTTP re-download instead of an unsafe resume.

Unsloth: Could not pre-download Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B
(AssertionError: daemonic processes are not allowed to have children);
continuing with the normal load.
```

The GPU was not out of memory:

```text
GPU Memory [Before loading Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B]
ROCM (AMD Radeon PRO W7800 48GB):
0.03GB/47.98GB (0.1% used, 47.95GB free)
```

## Model and operation involved

- Base model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`
- Operation: Studio inference model startup
- Also observed when loading a local LoRA adapter based on this model
- Model revision: `c202236235762e1c871ad0ccb60c8ee5ba337b9a`

The four cached weight shards matched the remote revision and remote sizes. An official cache verification reported only five small missing files:

```text
.gitattributes
LICENSE
README.md
merges.txt
vocab.json
```

After downloading only those five files, the official verification passed:

```text
repo_id=Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B repo_type=model checked=16
revision=c202236235762e1c871ad0ccb60c8ee5ba337b9a
```

Again, the intermittent successful load occurred before this manual cache completion, so this is diagnostic evidence rather than a confirmed workaround.

The successful local LoRA load took 61.2 seconds and ended with:

```text
Successfully loaded model
GPU Memory [After loading]: 17.67GB/47.98GB
Inference subprocess ready, entering command loop
```

## Additional context

The HTTP fallback error is similar to the open Hugging Face Hub issue about large downloads failing without an automatic retry:

https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/issues/4349

Potential improvements:

1. Do not force-download already valid cached weight shards when only small ancillary files are missing.
2. Retry or resume `httpx.RemoteProtocolError` failures for large shards.
3. Avoid the `daemonic processes are not allowed to have children` pre-download path.
4. Report the real state and progress in the Studio UI.
5. Clear or update the “Starting model” toast when the backend has already loaded the model.

No Hugging Face token, local username, chat content, dataset, or private prompt is included in this report.

title: [Feature Request] Unsloth Desktop as thin client for a remote Unsloth server (remote code execution like Codex/Claude Code)
body:
## Summary

Use **Unsloth Desktop as a thin client for a remote Unsloth server**, instead of (or in addition to) running models on the local machine. Today Desktop runs/loads models locally and only *points inference* at a remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint for chat. I'd like first-class support for:

1. **Pointing Desktop at a remote Unsloth/Unsloth-Studio instance** (my own dev server) where the models already live and are served, and using Desktop only as the UI.
2. **Running tools & code execution on that remote server** (like Codex / Claude Code do over SSH), so bash/python, file edits and deploys happen on the server, not on the local desktop — not just sending chat messages to a remote endpoint.

## Use case

I run several Qwen3.x GGUF models on a headless **dev server** (the machine with the GPU/CPU/RAM), which already exposes an OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint. I want to drive them from Unsloth Desktop running on my laptop:

- Desktop connects to the server's `/v1` endpoint for **inference** (this part partially works today via the remote-endpoint setting).
- But the **code execution / sandbox / file tools** still run locally on Desktop. I want those to run **on the server** — e.g. write code in the Desktop chat, have it execute `bash`/`python` and edit files *on the server filesystem*, and see results, exactly like Codex's or Claude Code's remote/SSH mode.

title: Inspiration
body:
Hey, I just stumbed upon this. We have a very similar class in our code base - It might be helpful to look at some of the ideas we've been discussing:

- 1) We believe `since_date` should be inclusive and `until_date` should be exclusive. See here for more details on why this is a good idea: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9795391/is-there-a-standard-for-inclusive-exclusive-ends-of-time-intervals

- 2) I'm not sure about the `2012-02-01..2012-03-01` format. Is `..` standard? We've been using `self.parse(start, end)` instead.

- 3) `split_to` is great - it looks like you've done the same thing with `in_groups_of`. Keep that name, it's better.

- 4) Support for finding the`intersection` of two date ranges, as well as `subtracting` two date ranges could also be useful.

- 5) Finally, you might want to consider allowing open ended date ranges. This is something we are about to implement. Having a notion of "All future days from this date" or "All past days from this date" can be very useful.

I hope we can get this into ActiveSupport so we don't have to come up with our own classes all the time ;-)

```
module Umr
  class DateRange
    attr_reader :since_date # Inclusive
    attr_reader :until_date # Exclusive

    def initialize(since_date, until_date)
      raise "Invalid date range: #{since_date} ; #{until_date}" if since_date > until_date

      @since_date = since_date
      @until_date = until_date
    end

    def inclusive_since_date
      since_date
    end

    def exclusive_until_date
      until_date
    end

    def exclusive_since_date
      since_date.yesterday
    end

    def inclusive_until_date
      [until_date.yesterday, since_date].max
    end

    def inspect
      "#<Umr::DateRange #{since_date}, #{until_date}>"
    end

    def self.parse(since_date_str, until_date_str)
      new(Date.parse(since_date_str), Date.parse(until_date_str))
    end

    # TODO Change to take singular argument
    def split_to(timespan)
      return [] if @since_date == @until_date
      unit = timespan.to_s.singularize
      end_date = [@since_date.send("next_#{unit}").send("at_beginning_of_#{unit}").to_date, @until_date].min
      [DateRange.new(@since_date, end_date)] + DateRange.new(end_date, @until_date).split_to(timespan)
    end

    def split_by(duration)
      return [] if @since_date == @until_date
      end_date = [@since_date + duration, @until_date].min
      [DateRange.new(@since_date, end_date)] + DateRange.new(end_date, @until_date).split_by(duration)
    end

    def in_days
      split_to('days')
    end

    def in_months
      split_to('months')
    end

    def in_weeks
      split_to('weeks')
    end

    def in_years
      split_to('years')
    end

    def size
      (until_date - since_date).to_i.days
    end

    def ==(other)
      @since_date == other.since_date && @until_date == other.until_date
    end

    def cover?(date)
      (since_date..until_date).cover?(date)
    end

    def intersection
    end

    def subtraction
    end

    def merge
    end
  end
end
```

title: [Feature Request]:  Support stateful ParDo, timers and @RequiresTimeSortedInput in the Spark Structured Streaming batch runner
body:
### What would you like to happen?

The Spark Structured Streaming (Dataset-based) runner currently rejects any `DoFn` that uses state, uses timers, or is annotated with `@RequiresTimeSortedInput`. `ParDoTranslatorBatch.canTranslate` fails with "States and timers are not supported for the moment", so the entire state and timer surface of the Beam model is unavailable on this runner.

The classic RDD-based Spark runner supports batch stateful ParDo, so this is a capability gap between the two Spark runners rather than a limitation of Spark.

### Proposal

Translate stateful / timer / time-sorted `ParDo` via `KeyValueGroupedDataset#flatMapSortedGroups`, grouping by key and ordering each group by event time, then drive the `DoFn` per key with `InMemoryStateInternals` and `InMemoryTimerInternals` from `runners-core`.

Because batch has no state store to bridge onto — state is a heap object scoped to one key — every Beam state type is already implemented by `InMemoryStateInternals`, so the state categories above can be enabled together rather than incrementally.

title: [Bug]: Transient connection error on worker fails all subsequent work items in CassandraIO read
body:
### What happened?

In `CassandraIO`, when a worker fails to connect to Cassandra database while processing a work item, it throws an exception (like `NoHostAvailableException`) [1] and the work item fails. However, it was observed that all the subsequent work items ran on the same worker fail immediately with an `IllegalStateException` [2] without even attempting to connect to the database. 

If a failed work item attempts all its leases on same worker, the entire job is failing due to a transient connectivity issue. 

[1] - Initial Exception
```com.datastax.driver.core.exceptions.NoHostAvailableException: All host(s) tried for query failed...
	at com.datastax.driver.core.ControlConnection.reconnectInternal(ControlConnection.java:270)  
	at com.datastax.driver.core.ControlConnection.connect(ControlConnection.java:109)  
	at com.datastax.driver.core.Cluster$Manager.negotiateProtocolVersionAndConnect(Cluster.java:1813)  
	at com.datastax.driver.core.Cluster$Manager.init(Cluster.java:1726)  
	at com.datastax.driver.core.Cluster.init(Cluster.java:214)  
	at com.datastax.driver.core.Cluster.connectAsync(Cluster.java:387)  
	at com.datastax.driver.core.Cluster.connect(Cluster.java:338)  
	at org.apache.beam.sdk.io.cassandra.ConnectionManager.lambda$getSession$3(ConnectionManager.java:78)  
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent(ConcurrentHashMap.java:1705)  
	at org.apache.beam.sdk.io.cassandra.ConnectionManager.getSession(ConnectionManager.java:76)```

[2] - Subsequent Exceptions (on same worker)
```java.lang.IllegalStateException: Can't use this cluster instance because it encountered an error in its initialization  
	at com.datastax.driver.core.Cluster.checkNotClosed(Cluster.java:650)  
	at com.datastax.driver.core.Cluster.connectAsync(Cluster.java:386)  
	at com.datastax.driver.core.Cluster.connect(Cluster.java:338)  
	at org.apache.beam.sdk.io.cassandra.ConnectionManager.lambda$getSession$3(ConnectionManager.java:78)  
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent(ConcurrentHashMap.java:1705)  
	at org.apache.beam.sdk.io.cassandra.ConnectionManager.getSession(ConnectionManager.java:76)```


### Issue Priority

comments: .take-issue

Triage : 

Ref - https://github.com/apache/beam/blob/master/sdks/java/io/cassandra/src/main/java/org/apache/beam/sdk/io/cassandra/ConnectionManager.java

- The cluster object is created during the first attempt by the worker and cached in a Map within ConnectionManager.(line 63)
- When `getSession` fails on an attempt (due to any transient issue on Cassandra), the broken Cluster object remains in the cache.
- If any other work item runs on the same worker, it fetches this cached cluster object. The Datastax driver checks it via `checkNotClosed()` and immediately fails it with an `IllegalStateException` because of the previous initialization failure.
- Because the broken connection is never evicted from the cache, a single transient failure permanently poisons the worker.

Proposed solution : 

- Check if the cached Cluster object is closed/broken before attempting to use it. 
- If it is broken, remove it from the map and compute a fresh one.

I will send a PR soon with the proposed change.

title: [Bug]: Java FlinkRunner OrderedListState silently overwrites duplicate elements sharing same timestamps
body:
### What happened?

## Component
runner-flink

## What happened?
When executing a pipeline using the `FlinkRunner` (specifically observed using the `HashMapStateBackend` / Java heap state configuration), adding multiple distinct elements with the **exact same timestamp** to an `OrderedListState` results in critical data loss. The last element written completely overwrites any previous elements that shared that specific millisecond timestamp bucket.

According to Beam's core architectural contract, `OrderedListState` should preserve and sort all appended values. It does not impose an invariant rule requiring timestamps to be globally unique. 

The underlying flaw stems from how `FlinkStateInternals` maps `OrderedListState` onto Flink's native primitive structures. The runner sets the key of Flink's internal tracking storage structure to the `Long` timestamp value itself. During back-to-back writes in a single execution bundle, the internal write-buffer performs a flat replacement (equivalent to a map `put` action) instead of appending the element to a sub-collection (like a `List`) associated with that timestamp bucket.

## Expected Behavior
`OrderedListState` should treat the timestamp solely as a sorting key index. If multiple elements share a timestamp, the runner's underlying serialization layout must wrap elements in an appendable multi-value collection (e.g., mapping to a Flink `MapState<Long, List<T>>`) so that subsequent writes do not execute a flat destructive overwrite.

## Actual Behavior
The second write (`"Ball"`) silently destroys and overwrites the initial write (`"Apple"`) at the timestamp boundary level inside the Java heap state backend.

## Environment
**Apache Beam Version:** 2.61.0
**Flink Version:** 1.19.1
**Runner:** FlinkRunner
**State Backend:** `HashMapStateBackend` (Java Heap)

### Issue Priority

Priority: 1 (data loss / total loss of function)

comments:
The problem is that `FlinkOrderedListState.readAsMap()` returns `Map<Instant, TimestampedValue<T>>`, which prevents multiple records with the same Instant. This would have to be changed to `MultiMap` , `PriorityQueue` or similar approach. Also there is missing `@ValidatesRunner` suite that will cover this behavior.

Overall (due to missing equivalent in Flink state primitives) the implementation is quite inefficient (mostly if the list grows larger), as it sorts the complete list on every `read()` or `readRange()`.

title: [Bug]:KafkaIO OAUTHBEARER auth against GCP Managed Service for Apache Kafka broken starting 2.69.0 (works on 2.68.0)
body:
### What happened?

KafkaIO OAUTHBEARER auth against GCP Managed Service for Apache Kafka broken starting 2.69.0 (works on 2.68.0)

Using Python `ReadFromKafka` with `sasl.mechanism=OAUTHBEARER` and
`sasl.login.callback.handler.class=com.google.cloud.hosted.kafka.auth.GcpLoginCallbackHandler`
to connect to **GCP Managed Service for Apache Kafka** from a Dataflow streaming job
(`DataflowRunner`, `--experiments=use_runner_v2`), the Kafka consumer fails 100% of
connection attempts with:

```
org.apache.kafka.common.errors.TimeoutException: Timeout expired while fetching topic metadata
  at org.apache.beam.sdk.io.kafka.KafkaIO$Read$GenerateKafkaSourceDescriptor...
```

with worker logs showing, for every connection attempt:

```
[Consumer clientId=..., groupId=...] Connection to node -1 (<broker>:9092) terminated
during authentication. This may happen due to any of the following reasons:
(1) Firewall blocking Kafka TLS traffic (eg it may only allow HTTPS traffic),
(2) Transient network issue.
```

This is **not** a network/firewall issue — same VPC/subnetwork/service-account/broker
worked correctly on Beam 2.68.0 and earlier.

## Bisection result

Tested directly against a live GCP Managed Kafka cluster (Dataflow, `DataflowRunner`,
identical pipeline code, identical JDK build (`17.0.18+8-Debian-1deb12u1`, controlled via
a pinned custom SDK container image so the JDK is not a variable), identical
`kafka-clients` (3.9.0) and identical `GcpLoginCallbackHandler.class` bytecode
(SHA256-verified) across every version tested:

| Beam version | Result |
|---|---|
| 2.67.0 | ✅ Works |
| 2.68.0 | ✅ Works (confirmed live data flowing) |
| **2.69.0** | ❌ **Fails** — 100% auth termination |
| 2.71.0 | ❌ Fails |
| 2.75.0 | ❌ Fails |

The break happens exactly between the **2.68.0 → 2.69.0** release.

## Dependency diff, 2.68.0 → 2.69.0

Diffing every `META-INF/maven/*/pom.properties` entry bundled in
`beam-sdks-java-io-expansion-service-{2.68.0,2.69.0}.jar`, after excluding
unrelated file-format IO connectors (ORC/Parquet/JTS, bundled in the same
shadowJar but irrelevant to Kafka), the changes touching the HTTP/auth path are:

```
org.apache.httpcomponents.client5:httpclient5   5.4.3 -> 5.5
io.confluent:kafka-schema-registry-client       7.6.1 -> 7.5.5   (downgrade)
io.confluent:common-utils                       7.6.1 -> 7.5.5   (downgrade)
net.bytebuddy:byte-buddy                        1.14.12 -> 1.17.7
```

`google-auth-library-oauth2-http` and `google-auth-library-credentials` are
**unchanged** across this specific boundary (both `1.37.1` / `1.30.0`), so this
looks like a transport-layer (`httpclient5`) or Confluent schema-registry-client
regression rather than a `google-auth-library` version bump, despite
`google-auth-library-oauth2-http` moving significantly (1.36.0 → 1.47.0) across
the wider 2.67.0 → 2.75.0 range.

## What's been ruled out

- `kafka-clients` version: identical (3.9.0) at every version tested
- `GcpLoginCallbackHandler.class`: byte-identical (SHA256-verified) at every version tested
- `managed-kafka-auth-login-handler` (Google's own artifact): identical, `1.0.5`
- JDK patch version: identical (`17.0.18+8-Debian-1deb12u1`), controlled via a pinned
  custom SDK container image built via multi-stage `COPY` from a known-good image,
  ruling out JDK/TLS-default drift as a factor
- Network/firewall/subnetwork/service account/IAM: identical config across all tests;
  ruled out because the *same* infra with only the Beam SDK version changed reproduces
  the failure deterministically

## Environment

- Runner: `DataflowRunner`, `--experiments=use_runner_v2`,
  `--dataflow_service_options=streaming_mode_at_least_once`
- SDK: Python 3.12, `apache-beam[gcp]`
- Kafka: GCP Managed Service for Apache Kafka, `SASL_SSL` + `OAUTHBEARER`
- Auth: `com.google.cloud.hosted.kafka.auth.GcpLoginCallbackHandler` (Application
  Default Credentials via the pipeline's attached service account)

## Reproduction

Minimal `consumer_config` used:

```python
{
    "bootstrap.servers": "<managed-kafka-bootstrap>:9092",
    "security.protocol": "SASL_SSL",
    "sasl.mechanism": "OAUTHBEARER",
    "sasl.login.callback.handler.class": "com.google.cloud.hosted.kafka.auth.GcpLoginCallbackHandler",
    "sasl.jaas.config": "org.apache.kafka.common.security.oauthbearer.OAuthBearerLoginModule required;",
}
```

Passed to `ReadFromKafka(consumer_config=consumer_config, topics=[...])` in a
streaming pipeline submitted with `--sdk_container_image` pinned to a custom image
per Beam version tested (JDK controlled/identical across all).

Happy to share the full bisection harness (build + throwaway-consumer-group test
script) if useful for reproducing this quickly across future release candidates.

title: Auto-link error where brackets are followed by the ellipsis character
body:
### URL

https://www.openstreetmap.org/changeset/186104937#c1628961

### How to reproduce the issue?

Example in a changeset comment, where the user writes:
`This change contains a way here (URI1)… and a way there (URI2).`

URI1 and URI2 are ordinary URI to OSM objects.
But the auto-generated hyperlink for URI1 incorrectly contains `)…`.

### Screenshot(s) or anything else?

_No response_
comments:
Auto linkification is, by definition, heuristic and will always get some edge cases wrong one way or another.

title: Remove SPA in favour of Rails conventions
body:
The closest I can find that mentions this is https://github.com/openstreetmap/openstreetmap-website/pull/4562. Also https://github.com/openstreetmap/openstreetmap-website/issues/6495 is a subset of this issue.

This app has historically used a lot of custom JS to make it work as an SPA. The core is [`OSM.Router`](https://github.com/openstreetmap/openstreetmap-website/blob/master/app/assets/javascripts/router.js), which handles pushState and renders the appropriate pages. This architecture has served us well for a long time, but gradually it has grown into a lot of JS that is not conventional to Rails and our maintainers don't necessarily understand very well. 

These days, a lot of our JS could be implemented using [Hotwire](https://hotwired.dev/), which is the current preference in the Rails ecosystem. We already use Hotwire in places. It's not all-or-nothing; we can get there in incremental steps (such as the mentioned https://github.com/openstreetmap/openstreetmap-website/issues/6495)

Note that we can't possibly handle everything with Hotwire. There will always be some custom JS, for example to handle the slippy map. However the closer we can get to Rails conventions, the easier it will be to maintain the app, as well as to attract new contributors.
comments: Isn't Hotwire's Turbo doing the opposite conversion from MPA to SPA?

I guess technically Turbo builds SPAs, but it does it in a way that is practically indistinguishable from building traditional, backend-rendered apps. It provides an abstraction that allows developers to mostly "build Rails", avoiding (or at least greatly reducing) custom JS such as our router.

Most importantly: it allows us to develop using Rails conventions, which are well documented and easier to onboard.
evidence: Remove SPA in favour of Rails conventions
These days, a lot of our JS could be implemented using [Hotwire](https://hotwired.dev/), which is the current preference in the Rails ecosystem.

title: Remove Sass/SCSS
body:
Based on a conversation started at https://github.com/openstreetmap/openstreetmap-website/issues/6679#issuecomment-3719742101 (plus that issue itself). Also mentioned at https://github.com/openstreetmap/openstreetmap-website/pull/7207#discussion_r3529179066

Part of what our asset pipeline does is turning Sass (technically SCSS) into standard CSS. This was very helpful in the past, when Sass could provide functionality that CSS didn't have, but CSS has grown a lot since then. These days it might be possible to drop Sass altogether, simplifying our asset handling requirements, moving towards standard and broadly-supported technologies, reducing our dependencies, and easing the barrier of entry to new contributors.

labels.name: refactor
labels.description: Refactoring, or things that work but could be done better

comments:
It would certainly be nice to drop the sass compilation chain, if that is possible. It's generally been a headache for us.

We're only light users of sass, and I think most of our usage can be split into the following categories:

* Sass usage that can be removed today. I think things like "$blue" are already available as CSS variables in Bootstrap 5.3
* Sass usage that can be removed in future. Bootstrap 6 is moving towards using CSS variables more extensively, and that may allow us to remove more sass variables.
* Sass usage that can be refactored. We use things like `@extend` and might be able to move this to classes in views, and other refactorings like that.
* Sass usage that might need workarounds. `media-breakpoint-up` is the most obvious one, since media breakpoints cannot be defined using variables. Unrolling sass loops might be another.

My recommendation would be to start refactoring the easy bits first, so that the rest of the discussion becomes more tractable. I would avoid the hard bits (e.g. the workarounds, or manually expanding loops, etc) for now since they are only a tradeoff that's worth doing when the goal is within reach.

title: Compress GPX files in the browser before upload
body:
https://github.com/openstreetmap/operations/issues/1378 reports GPX uploads failing with a 503 when the connection is slow, the likely cause is a timeout in Fastly/Apache, so the upload never finishes and the user just sees an error.

GPX is XML, so gzip cuts it by about 90%. A 1.5 MB file becomes around 150 kB. If the upload form compressed the file in the browser before sending, slow connections would have a much better chance to finish in time. This would help a lot in rural areas, where people often collect traces on poor mobile connections. Modern browsers have [CompressionStream built in](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CompressionStream), no extra library needed. If the browser doesn't support it, the form just uploads the raw file like today. The server already accepts .gpx.gz, so this change would only touch the upload form.

This is related to https://github.com/openstreetmap/openstreetmap-website/pull/7124, which adds gzip compression for plain GPX files on the server before they go to S3. In that PR the compression runs in Rails, so the server pays the CPU for it. If the browser sends the file already compressed, the server doesn't need to compress anything, and the upload itself is smaller too.
comments:
Would browsers not use a compressed transfer encoding anyway? I'm not really keen on trying to manually compress things in javascript.

What proportion of GPX uploads even use a browser I wonder?

> Would browsers not use a compressed transfer encoding anyway?

According to [deflate.conf.erb](https://github.com/openstreetmap/chef/blob/master/cookbooks/apache/templates/default/deflate.conf.erb), compression seems to be only for downloads. For uploads there is nothing automatic, the browser always sends the file raw.

> I'm not really keen on trying to manually compress things in javascript.

It is a native api now ([CompressionStream](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CompressionStream)), so it is a few lines of code, no library. If the browser doesn't support it, the form just uploads the raw file like today.

> What proportion of GPX uploads even use a browser I wonder?

I do not have  those numbers, maybe @Firefishy  could get those numbers.

title: documentation for requests.session.request(verify=...) duplicates requests.request() even where it is different
body:
[Docs currently state](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.Session.request):

 > Either a boolean, in which case it controls whether we verify the server’s TLS certificate, or a string, in which case it must be a path to a CA bundle to use. Defaults to True.

I suggest rewording both statements, because as they stand they make figuring what went wrong with setting the correct CA bundle way harder than it should be:

1. Passing bool not only controls *whether* the certificate is verified, it [also resets](https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/f43f750ee10addbaa13901c1017631b4d70fd6e3/src/requests/sessions.py#L74) the root store to be verified against.
2. The default for the *method* does **not** behave like True - leaving it unspecified simply defers to the session, as it should.. session in turn may very well have verify=False.
3. (still incomplete because of `os.environ` precedence, but I understand that one is currently #WONTFIX as per https://github.com/psf/requests/issues/3829)

## Documentation appears to state

|                |s.verify=True | s.verify="/S"|s.verify=False|
| -------------- |------------- |------------------- |------------------- |
| s.request(verify=True) | True         | ✅ "/S"              | True               |
| s.request(verify="/r") | "/r"         | "/r"               | "/r"               |
| s.request(verify=False)| False        | False              | False              |
| s.request() # i.e. s.request(verify=None) | True         | ⚠️True               | ⚠️True              |

## Actual Result

|                |s.verify=True | s.verify="/S"|s.verify=False|
| -------------- |------------- |------------------- |------------------- |
| s.request(verify=True) | True         | ⚠️True               | True               |
| s.request(verify="/r") | "/r"         | "/r"               | "/r"               |
| s.request(verify=False)| False        | False              | False              |
| s.request() # i.e. s.request(verify=None) | True         | ✅"/S"               | ✅ False              |

## Reproduction Steps

```python
>>> import certifi,requests,ssl,os
>>> certifi.__version__
'2026.04.22'
>>> certifi.where()
'/inaccessible/path'
>>> requests.__version__
'2.33.1'
>>> session = requests.session()
>>> session.verify = ssl.get_default_verify_paths().capath
>>> os.path.isdir(session.verify)
True
>>> session.request(url="https://example.com", method="HEAD")
<Response [200]>
>>> session.request(url="https://example.com", method="HEAD", verify=True)
Traceback (most recent call last):
[..]
  File "/home/user/lib/python3.10/site-packages/requests/adapters.py", line 304, in cert_verify
    raise OSError(
OSError: Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle, invalid path: /inaccessible/path
```

This result means that libraries that opt to use the supposedly-default parameter value of True are doing something meaningfully different from those that use the actual-default parameter of None (typically: by not mentioning the parameter).

## System Information

    $ python -m requests.help

```json
{
  "chardet": {
    "version": "4.0.0"
  },
  "charset_normalizer": {
    "version": "3.4.4"
  },
  "cryptography": {
    "version": ""
  },
  "idna": {
    "version": "3.3"
  },
  "implementation": {
    "name": "CPython",
    "version": "3.10.12"
  },
  "platform": {
    "release": "6.8.0-110-generic",
    "system": "Linux"
  },
  "pyOpenSSL": {
    "openssl_version": "",
    "version": null
  },
  "requests": {
    "version": "2.33.1"
  },
  "system_ssl": {
    "version": "30000020"
  },
  "urllib3": {
    "version": "2.6.3"
  },
  "using_charset_normalizer": false,
  "using_pyopenssl": false
}
```
comments:
Thanks for opening this issue, @biredel. `None` is not an intended value users should be passing for verify. I agree we could potentially reword the docstring though.

The current wording is intended to convey you do not need to pass a default, Requests will handle everything (which is what happens). If you choose to hardcode the documented default per request, you're encountering precedence decisions (explicit `request()` input will supercede `Session` settings).

If we changed it, it would probably be to convey it "defaults to the Session value, True by default".

## PR Submitted ✨

I've submitted a PR that addresses this documentation issue:

**PR:** https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/7403

**The fix:** Updated the verify parameter docstring in Session.request() to clarify that it defaults to the Session's verify value (which itself defaults to True), rather than saying it simply 'Defaults to True'.

This matches your suggestion: 'If we changed it, it would probably be to convey it defaults to the Session value, True by default.'

Happy to make any adjustments if needed!

title: mypy warns about invalid types for json argument
body:
<!-- Summary. -->

I have warnings about invalid types for the json argument, that didn't occur when using types-requests.

The changes in v2.34.1 changed the errors, but did not fix them.


<!-- What you expected. -->

```
typecheck.py:6: error: Argument "json" to "post" has incompatible type "dict[str, Collection[str]]"; expected "JsonType"  [arg-type]
typecheck.py:9: error: Argument "json" to "post" has incompatible type "dict[str, object]"; expected "JsonType"  [arg-type]
```

<!-- What happened instead. -->

## Reproduction Steps

```python
import requests

def fn(d: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    j = {"foo": d, "bar": "hi"}
    requests.post("https://example.com", json=j)

    k = {"foo": d, "bool": True}
    requests.post("https://example.com", json=k)

```

It seems ok if a literal is used without the intermediate variable:

```
    requests.post("https://example.com", json={"foo": d, "bar": "hi"})
    requests.post("https://example.com", json={"foo": d, "bool": True})
```

## System Information

```json
{
  "chardet": {
    "version": null
  },
  "charset_normalizer": {
    "version": "3.4.7"
  },
  "cryptography": {
    "version": ""
  },

    "version": "3.15"
  },

    "version": "3.13.5"

  "using_pyopenssl": false

```

<!-- This command is only available on Requests v2.16.4 and greater. Otherwise,
please provide some basic information about your system (Python version,
operating system, &c). -->
comments:
This looks like a current limitation of `mypy`. `pyright` and `ty` are both able to detect the typing is correct for these cases. `mypy` seems to be trying to group all possible types into the single highest common type. That's why we get `Collection[str]` and `object` neither of which is particularly helpful. In the context of calling Requests, it understands the types are compatible though.

The reason `types-requests` worked is because there was no type here, it was `Any`. We may have to degrade to shutting off typing to support `mypy` but I'd wanted to avoid that. Let me investigate a bit more to see if we can get something working.
I added explicit types to my intermediate variables as a solution for my case.

I think eventually we want to expose a subset of the types in _types.py publicly which would include `JsonType`. That would simplify manually typing input, but that's pretty poor ergonomics for using the `json` parameter. Given this affects 1 of 3 type checkers (but it's the most popular one), I think I'm going to leave this open for now.

I want to hopefully get some more data points on how much friction this is actually causing. I assume it'll be high but we should quantify that before making a decision. If it does prove to be a significant pain point, we'll look at moving to `Any`.

title: raise FileNotFoundError for missing TLS material
body:
Would you accept a PR which changes the existing OSError for missing TLS material to FileNotFoundError?

e.g.:

```
            if conn.cert_file and not os.path.exists(conn.cert_file):
                raise OSError(
                    f"Could not find the TLS certificate file, "
                    f"invalid path: {conn.cert_file}"
                )
```

becomes something like:

```
            if conn.cert_file and not os.path.exists(conn.cert_file):
                from errno import ENOENT
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    ENOENT,
                    "Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path",
                    str(conn.cert_file)
                )
```

Our use case is that there are temporary conditions where the files don't exist and it'd be nicer to handle FileNotFoundError specifically and be able to compare the .filename attribute rather than the more general OSError and test str(excp).endswith(...).  As FileNotFoundError is a subclass of OSError existing try/excepts continue to work but it would change the string representation:

```
>>> str(OSError("Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path: filename"))
'Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path: filename'
>>> str(FileNotFoundError(errno.ENOENT, "Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path", "filename"))
"[Errno 2] Could not find the TLS certificate file, invalid path: 'filename'"
```
comments:
If my read of the docs is accurate, this is a subclass of OSError so it's fine. The PR that was created is a spam automation that opened this before anyone agreed to it and they have opened more than 20 on other repos I've seen. 

If you'd like to send a PR for this @JKDingwall I'm happy to review this but please ensure you add unit tests for this change and update them.

I prepared the focused fix requested here and pushed it to my fork:

https://github.com/tomatotomata/requests/commit/be90ea47a5af638aeeac7f0e74dc55af3a11bc43

It changes the missing CA bundle, client certificate, and client key paths to raise `FileNotFoundError` with `errno.ENOENT` and the original path in `.filename`. The tests now check the specific exception and filename for all three cases.

Validation completed:

- `pre-commit run --files src/requests/adapters.py tests/test_requests.py`
- focused Requests tests: 2 passed
- `git diff --check`

The full `tests/test_requests.py` run reached 338 passed, but this Windows checkout does not materialize the repository's `tests/certs/valid/ca` symlink, so one unrelated TLS fixture could not run. The branch is `codex/file-not-found-tls-7564`. Requests does not allow me to create the PR directly, so this is ready for a maintainer to pull into review if the scope looks right.

@sigmavirus24 I've got round to testing my version of the change today: https://github.com/psf/requests/compare/main...JKDingwall:requests:7564-use-FileNotFoundError-for-missing-TLS-material?expand=1

This is largely the same as other versions that have been mentioned in the issue.  Some of my differences:

- When raising FileNotFound cast the path to `str(...)` in case a `pathlib.Path(...)` object has been passed.
```
>>> raise FileNotFoundError(errno.ENOENT, "message", pathlib.Path("/tmp"))
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] message: PosixPath('/tmp')
>>> raise FileNotFoundError(errno.ENOENT, "message", str(pathlib.Path("/tmp")))
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] message: '/tmp'
```

- In the test assertions `2` is not hardcoded as the value of `ENOENT`, while this is a common value there is no guarantee ENOENT == 2.  There is a belt-and-braces approach to testing the exception raised, if it is ott then I could reduce that.

title: Support for HTTP Query Method
body:
Hi,

I wanted to ask the if maintainers have plans to support the newly proposed QUERY http method in the near future, as it has been awaited for more than a decade. We plan to use the method in our APIs going forward, albeit most use will be internal. I see requests is matured and in feature freeze at this time, I also understand that we can send arbitrary methods by supplying the name in the "request" method, tho it has a caveat [regarding redirections](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc10008#name-redirection).

I started some work on a fork. However before opening a PR, I wanted to make sure if you are open to contributions in this direction, as I have seen multiple recent rejections on the subject. (I have to add, rightfully so)
comments:
Hi @yamac-kurtulus, as you noted Requests already supports arbitrary HTTP Verbs through the `requests.request()` API. The redirection caveat is relatively trivial to handle as well, so Requests should be fully capable of supporting this as is.

QUERY is quite recent (it's only been a proposed standard for a few weeks). I don't think we plan to add an official API or specification specifics until we see how this gets implemented in common server frameworks and the actual adoption rate. Adding a formalized API is a long-lived maintenance contract that if we rush into is a net-negative for the library. We can revisit this topic in the future.

body:
<!-- Summary. -->
Old docs suggest to me that if ``False``, it won't be immediately be downloaded: https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/1f6589ec3a1ee910f9a65cc3ceac60b26677bc0e/src/requests/sessions.py#L605
```
        :param stream: (optional) whether to immediately download the response
            content. Defaults to ``False``.
```

whether to immediately download the response default anwer=False, so it won't immediately download the response. ```
        :param stream: (optional) Whether to use the streaming property. Defaults to ``False``.

title: Cookies are not sent when the URL contains credentials
body:
`requests` extracts credentials embedded in a URL and sends them as an
`Authorization` header, but the same URL then matches no cookie in the jar, so
cookies are silently omitted.

## Expected Result

A cookie scoped to `127.0.0.1` is sent for `http://user:pw@127.0.0.1:PORT/`,
just as it is for `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`. The userinfo component is not part
of the host (RFC 3986 §3.2), and cookie matching is on the host (RFC 6265).

## Actual Result

The `Authorization` header is sent, but `Cookie` is omitted:

```
without credentials  Authorization=None                  Cookie='sid=secret'
with credentials     Authorization='Basic dXNlcjpwdw=='  Cookie=None
```

The credentials are honoured for authentication, so the URL form is clearly
supported, but cookie matching on that same URL fails. No error or warning is
raised.

## Reproduction Steps

Run a local HTTP server that records the `Authorization` and `Cookie` request
headers it receives. Create a `Session` and set a cookie on it scoped to
`domain="127.0.0.1"`, `path="/"`. Issue two GETs against the server: one to
`http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`, and one to `http://user:pw@127.0.0.1:PORT/`. The
first arrives with the `Cookie` header set and no `Authorization`; the second
arrives with `Authorization` set and no `Cookie`.

## System Information

```json
{
  "chardet": {"version": null},
  "charset_normalizer": {"version": "3.5.1"},
  "cryptography": {"version": ""},
  "idna": {"version": "3.18"},
  "implementation": {"name": "CPython", "version": "3.14.7"},
  "platform": {"release": "25.6.0", "system": "Darwin"},
  "pyOpenSSL": {"openssl_version": "", "version": null},
  "requests": {"version": "2.34.2"},
  "system_ssl": {"version": "30600030"},
  "urllib3": {"version": "2.7.0"},
  "using_charset_normalizer": true,
  "using_pyopenssl": false
}
```
