title: [Bug]:DockerSandbox：uploadFiles 把 base64 文件内容拼进 docker exec 的单个 argv，大文件必报「参数列表过长」(error=7)，导致 ToolResultEvictionMiddleware 静默失效
body:
**Describe the bug**

`SandboxBackedFilesystem.uploadFiles` 的兜底路径会把整个文件内容 base64 编码后拼进一条 shell 命令字符串：

```java
String cmd = "mkdir -p $(dirname " + escapedPath + ") && "
        + "printf '%s' '" + base64Content + "' | base64 -d > " + escapedPath;
```

随后 `DockerSandbox.doExec` 把这整条字符串作为**单个 argv 参数**传给 `ProcessBuilder("docker", "exec", "-w", root, containerId, "sh", "-c", command)`。

由于 `DockerSandbox` 没有实现 `SandboxFileTransfer` 接口，Docker 沙箱的文件上传**只有**这一条路可走。结果是：只要文件内容 base64 后超过操作系统的命令行/参数长度上限，`ProcessBuilder.start()` 就直接失败：

- **Windows**：`CreateProcess` 整条命令行上限 32,767 字符 → 约 24 KB 以上的文件必失败。
- **Linux**：`MAX_ARG_STRLEN` 单个参数上限 128 KB → 约 96 KB 以上的文件必失败。

影响最大的后果是：**`ToolResultEvictionMiddleware` 永远无法落盘真正的大工具结果**。该中间件只对超过 `maxResultChars` 的结果触发，而这些恰恰就是会超出 argv 上限的内容。写盘失败后 `maybeEvict` 打一条 WARN 并返回 `null`，超大结果原样留在模型上下文里。也就是说，落盘瘦身功能对它本来要处理的大结果完全不起作用，且失败是静默的，上下文持续膨胀。

`downloadFiles` 反方向也有同样的设计问题（内容以 base64 走捕获的 stdout 返回，还受 512 KB 的 `OUTPUT_TRUNCATE_BYTES` 截断，更大的文件会被截坏），不过硬失败的是上传这条路。

**To Reproduce**

1. 构建一个使用 `DockerSandbox` 作为文件系统后端、并启用默认 `ToolResultEvictionMiddleware` 的 agent（或直接调用 `AbstractFilesystem.write`）。
2. 让任意工具返回一个大文本结果（Windows 上 > 30 KB、Linux 上 > 100 KB 即可），触发中间件将其落盘到 `{evictionPath}/{agent}/{toolCallId}-{hash}`。
3. `uploadFiles` 报 `IOException: Cannot run program "docker": error=7`，落盘永远不会成功。

**Expected behavior**

文件内容应当通过 stdin 流式写入容器，而不是嵌进 argv——`DockerSandbox.doHydrateWorkspace` 自己就已经在用这个方案（`docker exec -i <container> tar -xf - -C <root>`，字节写进子进程 stdin）。例如可以让 `DockerSandbox` 实现 `SandboxFileTransfer`：

- `uploadFile`：`docker exec -i <container> sh -c 'mkdir -p "$(dirname <path>)" && cat > <path>'`，字节从 stdin 灌入——没有长度上限，也没有 base64 膨胀。
- `downloadFile`：`docker exec <container> cat <path>`，从 stdout 读原始字节，不走面向文本的截断逻辑。

这样任意大小的上传都能成功，`ToolResultEvictionMiddleware` 也能真正把大工具结果落盘。

**Error messages**

```
[sandbox-fs] uploadFiles failed for path: large_tool_results/<agent>/<toolCallId>-<hash>
java.io.IOException: Cannot run program "docker": Exec failed, error: 7 (参数列表过长)
	at java.base/java.lang.ProcessBuilder.start(ProcessBuilder.java:1170)
	at java.base/java.lang.ProcessBuilder.start(ProcessBuilder.java:1089)
	at io.agentscope.harness.agent.sandbox.impl.docker.DockerSandbox.doExec(DockerSandbox.java:152)
	at io.agentscope.harness.agent.sandbox.AbstractBaseSandbox.exec(AbstractBaseSandbox.java:176)
	at io.agentscope.harness.agent.filesystem.sandbox.SandboxBackedFilesystem.uploadFiles(SandboxBackedFilesystem.java:125)
	at io.agentscope.harness.agent.filesystem.sandbox.BaseSandboxFilesystem.write(BaseSandboxFilesystem.java:187)
	at io.agentscope.harness.agent.middleware.ToolResultEvictionMiddleware.maybeEvict(ToolResultEvictionMiddleware.java:200)
	at io.agentscope.harness.agent.middleware.ToolResultEvictionMiddleware.evictMessage(ToolResultEvictionMiddleware.java:158)
	at io.agentscope.harness.agent.middleware.ToolResultEvictionMiddleware.evictMessages(ToolResultEvictionMiddleware.java:125)
	at io.agentscope.harness.agent.middleware.ToolResultEvictionMiddleware.onReasoning(ToolResultEvictionMiddleware.java:94)
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- AgentScope-Java Version: 2.0.1（实际复现版本）；已确认 2.0.2-subagent-bugfix 仍存在——其发布的 sources jar 中 `SandboxBackedFilesystem.java` 与 `DockerSandbox.java` 和 2.0.1 完全一致
- Java Version: 17
- OS: Windows 11（Docker Desktop）；Linux 主机同样可复现，只是阈值更高（单参数 128 KB 上限）

**Additional context**

- 这个失败对 agent 来说是静默的：`FileUploadResponse.fail` → `maybeEvict` 返回 `null` → 超大工具结果原样留在上下文。虽然不会造成数据损坏，但落盘瘦身功能对它本来针对的大结果完全失效，长会话的 token 消耗被持续放大。
- `SandboxFileTransfer` 接口已经存在，且 `SandboxBackedFilesystem` 在沙箱实现了该接口时会优先走原生传输——问题只在于 `DockerSandbox` 没有实现它，导致永远落到 base64-over-argv 的兜底路径。
```

title: [Bug]:agentscope-service: frontend/src/features/build/ 目录中文件被gitignore中build/排除，导致页面未提交至代码库
body:
Bug 描述

  agentscope-service 前端目录 frontend/src/features/build/ 下的源代码从未被提交到 git 仓库。根目录 .gitignore 中存在一条通用的 build/ 忽略规则（原本用于忽略
  Gradle/Java 的构建输出目录），它会匹配仓库中任意名为 build 的目录，包括前端源码目录 src/features/build/。虽然 .gitignore 为 Java 路径添加了
  !**/src/main/**/build/ 和 !**/src/test/**/build/ 例外，但没有为前端的 src/features/build/ 添加例外，导致该目录被静默忽略。

  因此全新 clone 仓库后，frontend/src/main.tsx 和 frontend/src/pages/AgentsHubPage.tsx 引用的两个模块不存在，前端无法构建：

  - ./features/build/deployments/DeploymentsPage
  - ../features/build/agents/AgentsHubPage（AgentsHubPage 是应用首页，/ 路由会重定向到 /agents）

  该问题从初始提交 e5d5cf87（"Land Managed Agents service stack with Go aistio control plane."）起就存在。

  复现步骤

  1. 全新 clone 仓库：
  git clone https://github.com/agentscope-ai/agentscope-java.git
  cd agentscope-java/agentscope-service/frontend
  2. 安装依赖并执行构建：
  npm install
  npm run build
  3. 查看 TypeScript 编译报错。

  预期行为

  npm run build（即 tsc --noEmit && vite build）应成功完成类型检查并产出 aistio/ui/ 静态资源，src/features/build/ 下的源码应随仓库一起分发。

  错误信息

  > agentscope-service-frontend@0.1.0 build
  > tsc --noEmit && vite build

  src/main.tsx:54:29 - error TS2307: Cannot find module './features/build/deployments/DeploymentsPage' or its corresponding type declarations.

  54 import DeploymentsPage from './features/build/deployments/DeploymentsPage';
                                 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

  src/pages/AgentsHubPage.tsx:17:25 - error TS2307: Cannot find module '../features/build/agents/AgentsHubPage' or its corresponding type declarations.

  17 export { default } from '../features/build/agents/AgentsHubPage';
                             ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

  Found 2 errors in 2 errors.

  Errors  Files
       1  src/main.tsx:54
       1  src/pages/AgentsHubPage.tsx:17

环境信息

  - AgentScope-Java 版本：2.0.3-SNAPSHOT（commit 2c6977c4；bug 自初始提交 e5d5cf87 起存在）
  - Java 版本：17.0.19（前端构建本身不依赖 Java，但部署 aistiod 镜像需要）
  - 操作系统：macOS（Darwin 25.4.0）
  - Node / npm：v26.7.0 / 11.19.0
  - TypeScript：5.9.3（package.json 声明 ^5.7.2）；Vite 6.4.3

  附加信息

  受影响的文件/目录：

  - 根目录 .gitignore 第 27 行 build/ 规则缺少前端源码路径的例外。
  - 缺失目录：agentscope-service/frontend/src/features/build/，至少包含：
    - agents/AgentsHubPage.tsx（被 src/pages/AgentsHubPage.tsx 以 barrel re-export 方式引用，并在 main.tsx 中用于 /agents 路由）
    - deployments/DeploymentsPage.tsx（在 main.tsx 中用于 /deployments 路由）
    - 该目录下可能还存在其他未被引用到的子模块（api、components、子页面等），需从初始提交者或其他备份处恢复完整源码。

  建议修复方式：

  1. 在 .gitignore 中为前端源码目录添加例外：
  gitignore
  build/
  !**/src/main/**/build/
  !**/src/test/**/build/
  !**/frontend/src/features/build/
  !**/frontend/src/features/build/**
  2. 将 src/features/build/ 下缺失的源文件补回仓库（这些文件目前只存在于初始提交者的工作区，无法从 git 历史恢复）。
  3. （可选）考虑将过宽的 build/ 规则收窄为 /build/ 或 **/build/ 配合精确例外，避免未来再次误匹配源码目录。

title: [Bug]: RAGFlowConfig.rerankId uses Integer type but RAGFlow API expects String (model ID)
body:
## Describe the bug

In `agentscope-extensions-rag-ragflow` 2.0.2, the `RAGFlowConfig` class defines `rerankId` as `Integer`, but RAGFlow's `/api/v1/retrieval` API expects `rerank_id` to be a **String** (the rerank model ID, e.g. `"BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3@BAAI"` or a UUID hex string like `"b2a62730759d11ef987d0242ac120004"`).

This makes it impossible to use the rerank feature via the Java SDK, because there is no way to pass a valid RAGFlow rerank model ID.

## To Reproduce

1. Configure a rerank model in RAGFlow (e.g. `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` via SiliconFlow).
2. Try to set the rerank model ID in `RAGFlowConfig`:
   ```java
   RAGFlowConfig config = RAGFlowConfig.builder()
       .baseUrl("http://localhost:9380")
       .apiKey("ragflow-xxx")
       .datasetIds(List.of("abc123"))
       .rerankId(???)  // <-- expects Integer, but RAGFlow needs a String model ID
       .build();
3. There is no valid Integer value that corresponds to a RAGFlow rerank model.
Expected behavior
rerankId should be of type String to match RAGFlow's API contract.
Root cause analysis
- SDK code (RAGFlowConfig.java:76):
private final Integer rerankId;
Builder:
public Builder rerankId(Integer rerankId) { ... }
- RAGFlow server (api/db/db_models.py):
# In Tenant model:
rerank_id = CharField(max_length=128, null=False, help_text="default rerank model ID")
# In Dialog model:
rerank_id = CharField(max_length=128, null=False, help_text="default rerank model ID")
RAGFlow uses string-based model identifiers (e.g. "BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3@BAAI"), not integer IDs.
- Request body (RAGFlowClient.java:167-169):
if (config.getRerankId() != null) {
    requestBody.put("rerank_id", config.getRerankId());
}
This sends an Integer in the JSON body where RAGFlow expects a String.
Fix
Change rerankId from Integer to String in:
1. RAGFlowConfig field declaration
2. RAGFlowConfig.getRerankId() return type
3. RAGFlowConfig.Builder.rerankId() parameter type
Environment
- AgentScope version: 2.0.2
- Module: agentscope-extensions-rag-ragflow
- RAGFlow version: latest (v0.x)

After checking the full test surface, this needs a wider API-compatibility decision than the small focused change I expected, so I'm stepping back and leaving it unclaimed rather than rushing a breaking change.

title: [Bug]: ReActAgent silently resets conversation memory when AgentStateStore throws (and drops the stack trace)
body:
**Describe the bug**

In `ReActAgent.loadOrCreateAgentStateForSlot` (agentscope-core, `ReActAgent.java:441-448`), the `catch (Exception e)` around state loading falls back to a brand-new empty `AgentState` for **any** exception thrown by the configured `AgentStateStore` — not just "state not found". A transient backend failure (Redis/MySQL blip, connection timeout, serialization error after an upgrade, etc.) is therefore indistinguishable from a genuinely fresh session: the agent continues this turn with empty conversation history, and on the next successful save it can overwrite the previously persisted state.

The same catch also logs `e.getMessage()` instead of `e`, so the stack trace is dropped. For exceptions whose `getMessage()` is null or terse (NPE, some Jackson `JsonMappingException` paths, timeout wrappers), the log line gives no place to start from.

Related but distinct: #2702 (onError path does not persist), #2475 (sessionId with `/` corrupts the slot), #2535 (stale stateCache write-back overwrites newer state). This one is the read-side complement.

**To Reproduce**

1. Configure a `ReActAgent` / `HarnessAgent` with any `AgentStateStore` whose `getVersioned(...)` throws — e.g. a stub that simulates a transient `SQLException`/`RedisConnectionFailureException`:

   ```java
   AgentStateStore brokenStore = new AgentStateStore() {
       @Override
       public <T> Optional<VersionedState<T>> getVersioned(
               String userId, String sessionId, String key, Class<T> type) {
           throw new RuntimeException("simulated transient store failure");
       }
       // ... other methods delegate to a working in-memory store
   };
   ```

2. Put a few turns into a session so history exists in the working backend.
3. Make the backend throw once on the next `agent.call(...)` (flip a flag, kill the Redis proxy, etc.).
4. Send another message.

**Observed behavior**

- The turn proceeds as if the session were brand new; no prior messages are visible to the model.
- The only log line is:
  ```
  WARN  ReActAgent - Failed to load AgentState for slot (userId=alice, sessionId=demo): simulated transient store failure
  ```
  No stack trace.
- On the next successful save, the empty in-memory state can overwrite the previously persisted history.

**Expected behavior**

- A transient backend failure should propagate (or the turn should fail fast) rather than silently treating the session as new — the cost of a failed turn is much lower than the cost of silently wiping memory.
- The "fall back to a fresh state" path should be reserved for the genuine absence case, which the code already distinguishes (`versioned.isPresent()` / `legacy.found()` both return false without throwing).
- The log should include the exception itself (`log.warn("...", e)`), not just `e.getMessage()`.

**Error messages**

```
WARN  i.a.core.ReActAgent - Failed to load AgentState for slot (userId=alice, sessionId=demo): simulated transient store failure
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- AgentScope-Java Version: `2.0.3-SNAPSHOT` (main, commit `49cffeb6`)
- Java Version: 17
- OS: macOS 15.3 (darwin)

**Additional context**

The offending block is `ReActAgent.java:441-448`:

```java
} catch (Exception e) {
    log.warn(
            "Failed to load AgentState for slot (userId={}, sessionId={}): {}",
            userId,
            sessionId,
            e.getMessage());
    long version = stateStore.supportsVersioning() ? 0L : AgentStateStore.UNVERSIONED;
    return new VersionedState<>(fresh, version);
}
```

Happy to send a PR once we agree on the desired semantics — my one-line hypothesis is that the catch should (a) log `e` for the stack trace and (b) only return `fresh` when the exception is a known "not found" signal from the store, letting storage/serialization errors bubble.

title: [Bug]: WorkspaceTaskRepository orphan sweeper and heartbeat fail under sandbox filesystem
body:
**Describe the bug**

When a `HarnessAgent` is configured with a sandbox-backed filesystem (e.g. `SandboxBackedFilesystem` via the sandbox lifecycle middleware), the background maintenance threads of `WorkspaceTaskRepository` (`ws-task-maint-*`) cannot persist or read task records. The sandbox instance is injected into the filesystem only during an agent call (`SandboxLifecycleMiddleware.acquireForCall` → `setSandbox`, cleared in `releaseForCall`), but the heartbeat and orphan sweeper run on a standalone daemon thread with `sandbox == null`. As a result:

- The orphan sweeper throws `SandboxException.SandboxConfigurationException: No active sandbox — sandbox filesystem used outside of a call context` every sweep cycle and only logs a warning, so **orphaned tasks are never marked FAILED**.
- The heartbeat silently fails the same way (caught at `debug` level), so **`lastUpdatedAt` is never refreshed and RUNNING tasks never progress** — the whole task-liveness mechanism is broken in sandbox mode.

**To Reproduce**

1. Configure `HarnessAgent`/`ReActAgent` with a sandbox-backed workspace (sandbox mode + `SandboxBackedFilesystem`).
2. Submit an async background subagent task (`timeout_seconds=0`) via `AgentSpawnTool`.
3. Observe logs every ~5 min:

```
[ws-task-maint-176] WARN i.a.h.a.s.t.WorkspaceTaskRepository: - Orphan sweeper encountered an error: No active sandbox — sandbox filesystem used outside of a call context
```

**Expected behavior**

Task records are cross-call orchestration metadata and must not depend on a per-call sandbox instance. The sweeper should detect and mark orphaned tasks as `FAILED`, and the heartbeat should refresh `lastUpdatedAt` even when no agent call is in progress.

**Root cause (code pointers)**

- `io.agentscope.harness.agent.filesystem.sandbox.SandboxBackedFilesystem#requireSandbox` (line ~194) throws when `sandbox == null`.
- `WorkspaceTaskRepository#sweepOrphanedTasks` calls `WorkspaceManager#listAllTaskRecords` → `filesystem.glob(...)` on the maintenance thread.
- `WorkspaceManager` task-record paths (`readTaskMap`/`persistTaskMap`/`listAllTaskRecords`) route through the filesystem layer (`readWithOverride`/`writeUtf8WorkspaceRelative`), which requires a live sandbox.
- `SandboxLifecycleMiddleware` sets/clears the sandbox only around `ReActAgent.beforeAgentExecution`/`afterAgentExecution`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- AgentScope-Java Version: latest (2.0.3-SNAPSHOT)
- Java Version: TBD
- OS: Linux

**Additional context**

The `ControlPlaneTaskRepository` (aistio) is not affected because it persists via the control-plane HTTP API and has no client-side sweeper.

title: [Bug]: Sandbox workspace persistence fails silently on 307 redirect from gateway
body:
**Summary**

Sandbox workspace persistence via file API (`GET /download/{path}`) fails silently when the gateway returns HTTP 307 redirect, causing workspace snapshots to be lost after sandbox teardown.

**Root Cause**

1. `SandboxConnector` explicitly configures `HttpClient.Redirect.NEVER` (lines 93, 117 in `SandboxConnector.java`)
2. `Filesystem.read()` treats any non-2xx response (including 307) as failure (lines 124-128 in `Filesystem.java`)
3. Paths like `.agentscope-tmp/ws-persist-*.tar` are URL-encoded → `%2F` → triggers gateway normalization redirect
4. The exception is caught and logged as WARN in `SandboxManager.release()`, but COS snapshot upload never happens

**Impact**

- **Silent data loss**: users' workspace changes are lost after sandbox eviction
- Affects all deployments where sandbox access goes through a gateway that returns 307 for paths with `%2F`
- Only `download` API is proven affected; `upload` (POST with no path parameter) likely unaffected

**Reproduction**

```bash
curl -vk "{apiUrl}/download/.agentscope-tmp%2Fsome-file" -o /dev/null
# Observe: 307 redirect → Location header with decoded path
```

**Proposed Fix**

Change `SandboxConnector.java` (both constructors):

```java
.followRedirects(HttpClient.Redirect.NEVER)  →  .followRedirects(HttpClient.Redirect.NORMAL)
```

**Safety verification**:
- `NORMAL` does not follow redirects for requests with body (POST exec, multipart upload) → no regression
- `NORMAL` does not downgrade HTTPS→HTTP
- Download endpoint has no auth → losing auth header on redirect is safe

**Workaround** (application layer)

Override `KubernetesSandbox.doPersistWorkspace()` to catch `SandboxRequestException` and fall back to exec-based transfer (`tar -cf - | base64`).

**Environment**

- AgentScope Java: 2.0.1 (verified also present in main branch 2.0.3-SNAPSHOT)
- Deployment: Kubernetes sandbox with gateway routing

**Evidence Chain**

| Evidence | Source Location | Status |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| HttpClient configured with `Redirect.NEVER` | `SandboxConnector.java:93, 117` | ✅ Confirmed |
| Non-2xx treated as failure | `Filesystem.java:124-128` | ✅ Confirmed throws `SandboxRequestException` |
| Path URL encoding produces `%2F` | `Filesystem.java:121` calls `percentEncode()` | ✅ Confirmed |
| Retry whitelist excludes 3xx | `SandboxConnector.java:50` | ✅ Only 500/502/503/504 |

Discovered through production run log analysis showing:
```
SandboxLifecycleMiddleware.releaseForCall
→ SandboxManager.release
→ KubernetesSandbox.doPersistWorkspace
→ Filesystem.read
→ HTTP 307 → "Download failed (status=307)" → SandboxRequestException
→ COS snapshot upload not executed
```

title: [Bug]: ReActAgent treats thinking-only final response as finished - user receives no text message, silent failure
body:
**Summary**

When a reasoning model occasionally emits its entire final answer in the `reasoning_content` channel with empty `content` (`finish_reason=stop`, no tool calls), `ReActAgent` judges the run as finished. The final message contains only a `ThinkingBlock` and no `TextBlock`, so AG-UI emits zero `TEXT_MESSAGE_*` events and the persisted assistant turn has no text. No error, no warning - a silent empty reply.

Observed in production with kimi-k2.6 (DashScope OpenAI-compatible endpoint); intermittent - the same session's previous identical round produced normal text.

**Root Cause** (verified on main @ 49cffeb6, 2.0.3-SNAPSHOT)

| Link | Location | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Response parsing | `OpenAIResponseParser.java:431-466` | `reasoning_content` -> `ThinkingBlock`; empty `content` -> no `TextBlock` (faithful parsing, correct) |
| Event emission | `ReActAgent.java:2550-2562` (`emitBlockEvents`) | `TextBlock` -> `TextBlock*Event`; nothing emitted for text when absent |
| Finish check | `ReActAgent.java:3682-3693` (`isFinished`) | `return toolCalls.isEmpty();` - never checks that the final response contains user-visible content |
| AG-UI conversion | `TextBlockEventConverter.java:33-40` | `TextMessage*` events sourced exclusively from `TextBlock*` events |

A final assistant message consisting solely of a `ThinkingBlock` therefore passes `isFinished()` and terminates the ReAct loop with an empty visible reply.

**Impact**

- User gets no answer and no error (run finishes "successfully"); nothing at WARN/ERROR level to alert on
- Assistant turn persisted without text (reasoning only), degrading subsequent multi-turn context
- Affects any reasoning model on the OpenAI-compatible path using `reasoning_content` (kimi-k2 confirmed; DeepSeek-R1-class models share the same risk)
- Intermittent and model-dependent - hard to detect from logs

**Production Evidence**

One run: 6 model calls, 5 tool calls all successful; final generation produced 170 output tokens entirely in reasoning parts, `finish_reason=stop`; trace output parts were `[{"type":"reasoning", ...}]` with no text part. Full AG-UI event stream for the run: `TEXT_MESSAGE*` count = 0 (thinking stream normal), then `RunFinished`. Framework-level WARN/ERROR in the window: 0 - excluding retries/degradation/HTTP errors; purely a response-structure issue.

**Proposed Fix** (either or both)

1. **Built-in empty-final-response retry**: in the postReasoning pipeline, when the final response has no `ToolUseBlock` and no `TextBlock` (thinking-only), trigger the existing `gotoReasoning` mechanism with a nudge message (e.g. "your previous reply had empty content; write the final answer in the content channel"), with a retry cap. The machinery already exists (`ReActAgent.java:2416-2422`) - it is just not used for this case.
2. **Stricter finish check**: `isFinished()` additionally requires a non-empty user-visible block. Riskier as a hard rule - may break legitimate non-text finals (structured output etc.), so direction 1 is safer.

At minimum, a WARN log on "final response has no visible content" would make this detectable.

**Workaround** (application layer)

A PostReasoning middleware performing the check + `gotoReasoning` described in direction 1 - works on 2.0.1 without framework changes.

**Environment**

- AgentScope Java: 2.0.1 (production); verified still present in main 2.0.3-SNAPSHOT @ 49cffeb6
- Model: kimi-k2.6 via DashScope OpenAI-compatible endpoint
evidence: [Bug]: ReActAgent treats thinking-only final response as finished - user receives no text message, silent failure
No error, no warning - a silent empty reply.

title: [Bug]: column "product_id" does not exist when querying product.options (*options) — 2.16+ ProductProductOption pivot mapping
body:
### Bug report

Querying products with the `options` relation expanded (e.g. `fields=id,*options` on `/store/products` or `/admin/products`, or the admin dashboard's product option UI) throws:

```
{"type":"invalid_data","message":"column p0.product_id does not exist"}
```

The exact alias in the error varies by call site (seen both `p0.product_id` and `o3.product_id` from the admin dashboard), but the failure is consistent: any query expanding `Product.options` fails.

### Root cause (as far as I can tell)

Since 2.16.0, `@medusajs/product` defines **two parallel relations** between `Product` and `ProductOption`:

```js
// product.js
options: model.manyToMany(() => ProductOption, {
  pivotEntity: () => ProductProductOption,
}),
product_options: model.hasMany(() => ProductProductOption, {
  mappedBy: "product",
}),
```

```js
// product-product-option.js (pivot entity, @since 2.16.0)
const ProductProductOption = model.define("ProductProductOption", {
  id: model.id({ prefix: "prodopt" }).primaryKey(),
  product: model.belongsTo(() => Product, { mappedBy: "options" }),
  product_option: model.belongsTo(() => ProductOption, { mappedBy: "products" }),
  values: model.manyToMany(() => ProductOptionValue, {
    pivotEntity: () => ProductProductOptionValue,
  }),
});
```

The `product_product_option` table itself has a correct `product_id` column (confirmed via `\d product_product_option` and a manual join, both work fine). But MikroORM's auto-generated join for the older `options` many-to-many relation (via `pivotEntity`) appears to build the query against the wrong table alias, producing a `product_id` reference on an alias that doesn't have that column — likely a collision between the `options` (manyToMany + pivotEntity) and `product_options` (hasMany, mappedBy: "product") relations pointing at the same pivot table.

### Reproduction

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:9000/store/products?limit=1&fields=id,*options' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: <key>'
# => {"type":"invalid_data","message":"column p0.product_id does not exist"}

# Works fine without *options:
curl 'http://localhost:9000/store/products?limit=1&fields=id,title'
curl 'http://localhost:9000/store/products?limit=1&fields=id,*variants'
curl 'http://localhost:9000/store/products?limit=1&fields=id,*variants.prices'

# Manual SQL confirms the data/schema is correct:
SELECT po.id, po.title, ppo.product_id
FROM product_option po
LEFT JOIN product_product_option ppo ON ppo.product_option_id = po.id
LIMIT 10;
-- returns correct rows
```

Also reproducible in the Admin dashboard UI (product option editing surfaces the same error client-side, e.g. `column o3.product_id does not exist`).

### Environment

- `@medusajs/medusa`: 2.19.0 (also present in 2.14.2, so this predates at least a few minor versions — possibly present since the 2.16.0 `product_options` refactor)
- Node: v22.22.1
- PostgreSQL: 18.4
- Package manager: pnpm 10.11.1

### Expected behavior

Expanding `*options` on a product query should return the product's options via the `product_product_option` pivot table without error, same as expanding `*variants` or `*categories` works today.

### Additional notes

- `db:migrate` reports the `product` module as fully up to date; this is not a missing-migration issue.
- The `options` field is not currently required by our storefront, so this is not blocking for us, but it does break admin UI functionality that relies on the option relation.
comments:
Thanks for reporting this! We've labeled it as a bug and will investigate.

Querying product options via the options relation (e.g. fields=*options on store/admin product endpoints) fails with a SQL error about a non-existent product_id column on an incorrect table alias. The root cause is confirmed in the codebase: Product defines two parallel relations to the same pivot table — a manyToMany to ProductOption via pivotEntity: ProductProductOption, and a hasMany directly to ProductProductOption (added in 2.16.0). ProductProductOption.product maps back via mappedBy: 'options', creating an ambiguous ORM mapping that causes MikroORM to generate invalid join SQL. This breaks all queries expanding options on products and also breaks the admin dashboard product option UI.

Investigated this. The straightforward fix (removing the seemingly-redundant `product_options: model.hasMany(...)` relation added in 2.16.0, since `options: model.manyToMany(...)` already exists) turns out to be more contested than it looks: `product-module-service.ts` explicitly references `"product_options"` by name in relation-exclusion logic (`relationsSet.delete("product_options")`, filters on `relation !== "product_options"`), suggesting this relation is deliberately handled elsewhere in the service layer rather than being an accidental duplicate. Removing it outright risks leaving that service-layer logic pointing at a relation that no longer exists.

Given that, this needs someone with more context on why `product_options` was added alongside `options` (possibly a v2.16.0 migration path, or intentional dual-relation modeling for a reason not obvious from the model file alone) to weigh in before a safe fix can be made. Flagging this contradiction here in case it helps whoever picks this up next avoid the same naive-removal trap.

debian:bookworm-slim

### Browser name

_No response_

### What happended?

When OpenTelemetry instrumentation is enabled, the root HTTP span closes as soon as
Express dispatches the request, not when the response is sent. Which causes:

1. `http.statusCode` attribute is `200` for every requests regardless of the actual status code.
2. Therefore, the span status is never `SpanStatusCode.ERROR`.
3. The root span duration excludes the work the request actually did.

This does await: https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/51c48dcb472c3b232b88337030945b2b651e90f8/packages/medusa/src/instrumentation/index.ts#L52-L63

But this doesn't and just return: https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/51c48dcb472c3b232b88337030945b2b651e90f8/packages/medusa/src/commands/start.ts#L259

Those above causes traces to be misleading.

### Expected behavior

1. `http.statusCode` attribute is `200` for every requests regardless of the actual status code.
2. Therefore, the span status is never `SpanStatusCode.ERROR`.
3. The root span duration excludes the work the request actually did.

### Actual behavior

1. `http.statusCode` reflects the actual status code in the respond
2. `SpanStatusCode.ERROR` is set when 500
3. The root span duration includes the whole request.

### Link to reproduction repo

None
comments:
Thanks for reporting this! We've labeled it as a bug and will investigate.

Confirmed bug in the OpenTelemetry HTTP instrumentation layer. In packages/medusa/src/commands/start.ts, traceRequestHandler is called with void (not awaited), and its inner async callback calls app(req, res) without waiting for the Express response lifecycle to complete. Since Express is callback-based, this async callback resolves immediately after dispatching, causing the OTel span to close before the response is actually written. As a result: (1) http.statusCode is always the value set at dispatch time (200) regardless of actual response status, (2) spans are never marked as ERROR for 5xx responses, and (3) span durations reflect only dispatch time rather than full request processing time. This affects all users of the OTel integration, making traces misleading. The fix would require the inner callback to await a Promise that resolves on res.once('finish') before the span closes.

`http.statusCode` attribute is `200` for every requests regardless of the actual status code.

title: [Bug]: Admin price-list quantity tiers are serialized as generic rules instead of native quantity fields
body:
### Package versions

```json
{
  "@medusajs/cli": "2.18.0",
  "@medusajs/framework": "2.18.0",
  "@medusajs/medusa": "2.18.0"
}
```

* Node.js: v25.9.0
* Database: PostgreSQL
* OS: Windows 11
* Browser: Chrome

### What happened?

Creating quantity-tier prices through the Medusa Admin price-list editor stores `min_quantity` and `max_quantity` as generic price rules instead of the native quantity fields on `Price`.

The Admin form appears to accept and display the tiers correctly, but the persisted price rows have:

```text
price.min_quantity = null
price.max_quantity = null
price.rules = { min_quantity: 5, max_quantity: 9 }
```

As a result, the tier is never selected during cart price calculation. The pricing repository removes `quantity` from the generic rule context and applies it specifically against `price.min_quantity` / `price.max_quantity`, which are null for prices created by this Admin flow.

This appears to originate in the Dashboard price-list form mapping:

* [`buildPriceRules` adds `min_quantity` and `max_quantity` to `rules`](<https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/develop/packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/price-lists/common/utils.ts#L312-L321>)
* [create/update price payloads send those `rules` without native `min_quantity` / `max_quantity` fields](<https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/develop/packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/price-lists/common/utils.ts#L357-L375>)
* [the form also moves native quantity fields into `rules`](<https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/develop/packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/price-lists/common/utils.ts#L85-L100>)

The core price-list workflow and pricing engine support native `Price.min_quantity` and `Price.max_quantity`; the problem appears limited to how the Admin serializes the tier form values.

### Expected behavior

Quantity tiers entered in the Admin price-list editor should be persisted as native price fields, for example:

```json
{
  "amount": 7000,
  "currency_code": "cad",
  "min_quantity": 5,
  "max_quantity": 9,
  "rules": {}
}
```

Adding 5-9 units of the variant to a cart should then select this price-list tier.

Leaving the non-tier/base price cell blank should also remain supported; it should not prevent independently configured tiers from matching.

### Actual behavior

The Admin persists an equivalent payload shaped like:

```json
{
  "amount": 7000,
  "currency_code": "cad",
  "rules": {
    "min_quantity": 5,
    "max_quantity": 9
  }
}
```

The resulting `Price` row has null native quantity boundaries. Cart pricing ignores the tier and falls back to another applicable price.

### Reproduction

1. Start a Medusa 2.18.0 application with the bundled Admin.
2. Create an active sale price list.
3. Add a product to it and open the **Prices** step.
4. Expand a variant's price cell.
5. Leave the main/base price blank.
6. Add tier prices such as `min quantity = 2, max quantity = 4` and `min quantity = 5, max quantity = 9`.
7. Save the price list.
8. Inspect the created prices through the Admin API or database. Their native `min_quantity` / `max_quantity` fields are null, while price rules named `min_quantity` / `max_quantity` were created.
9. Add a matching quantity to a cart. The tier price is not selected.

The same malformed persistence occurs for currency prices and region-rule prices. It does not require a customer-group rule.

### Related issue

This has the same visible symptom as medusajs/medusa#15994, but the reproduction here is narrower and points to a separate Dashboard serialization problem. The cart workflow in 2.18.0 already passes line-item quantity into price calculation; correcting the pricing-context TypeScript type alone does not change these malformed Admin-created price rows.

### Reproduction repository

No custom reproduction repository is required: the issue reproduces in a standard Medusa 2.18.0 application using the bundled Admin and the steps above. The linked `develop` source currently contains the serialization path described above.
comments:
Thanks for reporting this! We've labeled it as a bug and will investigate.

Confirmed bug in the Admin dashboard price-list editor: the buildPriceRules function and extractPriceDetails helper in packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/price-lists/common/utils.ts (lines ~95-100, 332-342, and 394-401) serialize min_quantity and max_quantity as generic price rules rather than as native top-level fields on the price payload. As a result, prices created or updated via the Admin UI have null native quantity boundaries, so the pricing engine never selects the tier during cart calculation. This is a separate issue from #15994 (which concerns the cart pricing context not passing quantity); here the prices themselves are persisted incorrectly. A fix requires updating the serialization path to include min_quantity and max_quantity as top-level fields on AdminCreatePriceListPrice / AdminUpdatePriceListPrice payloads.

### Expected behavior Quantity tiers entered in the Admin price-list editor should be persisted as native price fields, for example: ```json { "amount": 7000, "currency_code": "cad", "min_quantity": 5, "max_quantity": 9, "rules": {} } ``` Adding 5-9 units of the variant to a cart should then select this price-list tier.

title: [Bug]: Caching module invalidation is unbounded and runs on `worker_mode: server` processes, OOMing the API container under bulk writes
body:
### Package.json file

```JSON
 Relevant versions: `@medusajs/medusa` / `@medusajs/framework` 2.19.0, `@medusajs/caching-redis` ^2.19.0, `@medusajs/event-bus-redis` ^2.19.0.
```

### Node.js version

v22.18.0

### Database and its version

PostgreSQL 16.2

### Operating system name and version

Debian 12 (node:22-slim container), Linux host

### Browser name

_No response_

### What happended?


The Caching Module's automatic invalidation has two independent problems. Together they exhaust the Node heap of a self-hosted deployment during any burst of writes — in our case a catalogue sync through the Admin API, which killed the API container roughly 90 seconds after every boot.

**1. Clears are dispatched with `void`, so nothing can apply backpressure.**

`CachingModuleService.performCacheClear` (`dist/services/cache-module.js`, `src/services/cache-module.ts`):

```js
for (const providerId of providerIds_) {
  const provider = this.providerService.retrieveProvider(providerId);
  void provider.clear({ key, tags, options });   // <-- not awaited
}
```

Because of the `void`, the `await` in `clear_` resolves before Redis has done anything, and the `ongoingRequests` coalescing above it can never dedupe — the entry is deleted almost immediately. `performCacheSet` does the same with `provider.set(...)`.

For the `caching-redis` provider, one tag-based `clear` is an `SMEMBERS` per tag, then a `getBuffer` per member key under `Promise.all`. With a hot list tag such as `Product:list:*`, that set contains one member per cached list key. So each call materialises thousands of buffers, and N concurrent calls materialise N × that, with nothing limiting N.

**2. The invalidation handler is registered as an event-bus interceptor, so it runs in the emitting process.**

`DefaultCacheStrategy.onApplicationStart` (`dist/utils/strategy.js`, `src/utils/strategy.ts`):

```js
eventBus.subscribe("*", handleEvent);
eventBus.addInterceptor?.(handleEvent);
```

`subscribe` only runs where the BullMQ worker exists — `event-bus-redis` builds a worker only `if (this.isWorkerMode)`. But `addInterceptor` runs wherever an event is *emitted*: `RedisEventBusService.emit()` calls `eventsToEmit.forEach((eventData) => this.callInterceptors(eventData, ...))`, and `releaseGroupedEvents()` does the same. `AbstractEventBusModuleService.callInterceptors` maps over the handlers without awaiting them.

So a process started with `projectConfig.workerMode: "server"` — which is documented as not processing events — runs the full invalidation for every event it emits, i.e. for every write served by the Admin/Store API, while also serving HTTP traffic.

**3. The interceptor is also redundant.** In both `emit()` and `releaseGroupedEvents()`, every event is queued to BullMQ whenever a matching subscriber exists, and the strategy's own `subscribe("*")` guarantees the wildcard filter matches. So in a server/worker split, each event is invalidated twice: once in-process on the server via the interceptor, once on the worker via the queue.


### Expected behavior


- `worker_mode: "server"` processes do not run cache invalidation, or the interceptor path is reconciled with the `*` subscriber so each event is invalidated exactly once.
- Invalidation applies backpressure: `provider.clear(...)` is awaited (which also makes the existing `ongoingRequests` coalescing effective), and/or tags from a burst of events are batched into a bounded number of clears instead of one clear per event.

### Actual behavior

Under a bulk write burst (~10k products updated through the Admin API), the `server` container's heap climbs continuously and V8 aborts:

```
<--- Last few GCs --->
[20:0x31b25000]    88305 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 2023.7 (2075.3) -> 2021.1 (2076.5) MB, ...
[20:0x31b25000]    88629 ms: Scavenge (interleaved) 2024.8 (2076.5) -> 2023.5 (2096.8) MB, ...
<--- JS stacktrace --->
FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

Secondary symptoms before the crash:

- Unrelated request latency degrades from ~10 ms to 7.6 s as the event loop starves.
- The clears exceed `caching-redis`'s default 5 s `commandTimeout`. That is caught by `isConnectionError` and returned as a no-op, so invalidation aborts half-done: stale entries stay cached and their key names remain as orphaned members of the tag set, making every subsequent clear of that tag more expensive.

Setting `workerMode: "server"` does not avoid it, and there is no option to disable automatic invalidation — the `caching` feature flag only gates whether anything is *stored* (`useCache` / `@Cached`), while `onApplicationStart` wires invalidation unconditionally. Not registering the module at all is the only supported way to silence it, which also gives up caching.

Custom strategies would be the natural escape hatch, but they are currently disabled in `loaders/providers.js`:

```js
const strategy = strategy_1.DefaultCacheStrategy; // Re enable custom strategy another time
```

A `patch-package` patch against 2.19.0, if useful as a starting point:

1. `await provider.clear(...)` in `performCacheClear` instead of `void`.
2. Drop the `addInterceptor` registration (redundant with the `*` subscriber, per point 3).
3. Accumulate tags from events into a deduplicating `Set`, drained by one flush at a time in batches. In our workload the tags across a sync are nearly all duplicates, so tens of thousands of events collapse into a handful of clears.

After this, the same sync runs flat instead of OOMing.


### Link to reproduction repo

none
comments:
Thanks for reporting this! We've labeled it as a bug and will investigate.

Two confirmed bugs in the caching module cause unbounded memory growth and OOM crashes under bulk writes. First, performCacheClear (cache-module.ts:405) and performCacheSet (cache-module.ts:324) use void provider.clear()/set() instead of await, meaning the ongoingRequests coalescing map is deleted almost immediately and provides no deduplication — each event spawns unbounded concurrent Redis operations. Second, DefaultCacheStrategy.onApplicationStart (strategy.ts:95-96) registers both a wildcard subscriber AND an addInterceptor handler; the interceptor runs in-process on every emitting process including workerMode: 'server', so the server container performs full cache invalidation for every write it serves, defeating the server/worker split. The two paths also double-invalidate in a worker setup. Custom strategies — the natural escape hatch — are disabled in loaders/providers.ts:49. The reporter confirmed OOM crashes on a 2.19.0 deployment with a Redis caching…
